bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第135卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 135.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 135.

sentences.zh: 【齊紀一】起屠維協洽，盡昭陽大淵獻，凡五年。

translations.literal: [Qi Records 1] Beginning with tuyou xiehe, ending with zhaoyang dayuanxian — five years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Qi Records 1] From the year 479 through 483, five years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲辰，以江州刺史蕭嶷爲都督荊、湘等八州諸軍事、荊州刺史，尚書左僕射王延之爲江州刺史，安南長史蕭子良爲督會稽等五郡諸軍事、會稽太守。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the jiachen day, Xiao Yan, Governor of Jiangzhou, was made Commander-in-Chief of military affairs for Jing, Xiang, and six other provinces and Governor of Jingzhou; Wang Yanzhi, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, was made Governor of Jiangzhou; Xiao Ziliang, Senior Administrator of Annan, was made Commander-in-Chief of military affairs for Kuaiji and four other commanderies and Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first month's jiachen day, Xiao Yan was appointed to command the armies of eight provinces including Jing and Xiang and to govern Jingzhou; Wang Yanzhi became governor of Jiangzhou; and Xiao Ziliang was made military commander over five commanderies around Kuaiji and named its administrator.

sentences.zh: 初，沈攸之欲聚眾，開民相告，士民坐執役者甚眾，嶷至鎮，一日罷遣三千餘人。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shen Youzhi wished to gather troops, he had opened rewards for mutual informing among the people; very many gentry and commoners were detained for corvée labor. When Yan arrived at his post, in one day he dismissed more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi had been raising troops, he had encouraged citizens to inform on one another, and a great many people had been pressed into corvée. On reaching his command, Yan released more than three thousand of them in a single day.

sentences.zh: 府州儀物，務存儉約，輕刑薄斂，所部大悅。

translations.literal: The insignia and furnishings of the prefectural and provincial offices were kept to frugality; punishments were light and levies thin — the region was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He kept provincial regalia plain, lightened punishments and taxes, and his jurisdiction rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以竟陵世子賾爲尚書僕射，進號中軍大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Ze, heir of Jingling, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat; his title was advanced to Grand General of the Central Army and Director with protocols equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Ze, heir of the Prince of Jingling, was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and promoted to Grand General of the Central Army with an office equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 太傅道成以謝朏有重名，必欲引參佐命，以爲左長史。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Daocheng, because Xie Tiao had a great reputation, was determined to bring him in as a participant in founding the mandate, and appointed him Left Chief of Staff.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Daocheng, eager to enlist the celebrated Xie Tiao in the founding of the new order, made him his Left Chief of Staff.

sentences.zh: 嘗置酒與論魏、晉故事，因曰：「石苞不早勸晉文，死文慟哭，方之馮異，非知機也。」

translations.literal: Once he set out wine and discussed Wei and Jin precedents with him, saying: "Shi Bao did not urge Jin Wen early; when Wen died Bao mourned and wept. Compared with Feng Yi, this was not knowing the moment."
translations.idiomatic: Over wine he once discussed Wei and Jin history and remarked, "Shi Bao failed to press Sima Zhao in time; when Zhao died, Bao wept at his bier. Beside Feng Yi, that was not knowing when to act."

sentences.zh: 朏曰：「晉文世事魏寶，必將身終北面；

translations.literal: Tiao said: "Jin Wen had served Wei all his life; he would surely have ended his days facing north as a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao replied, "Sima Zhao had served Wei all his life and would surely have died facing north as its subject.

sentences.zh: 借使魏依康、虞故事，亦當三讓彌高。」

translations.literal: Even if Wei had followed the Yao and Shun abdication story, he still would have thrice declined and risen higher still."
translations.idiomatic: Even had Wei followed the abdication of Yao and Shun, he would still have declined the throne three times and risen all the higher."

sentences.zh: 道成不悅。

translations.literal: Daocheng was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng was displeased.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以朏爲侍中，更以王儉爲左長史。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Tiao was made Palace Attendant; Wang Jian replaced him as Left Chief of Staff.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Tiao was made Palace Attendant, and Wang Jian took his place as Left Chief of Staff.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以給事黃門侍郎蕭長懋爲雍州刺史。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Xiao Changmao, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate in the Secretariat Service, was made Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Xiao Changmao was appointed governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙子，邵陵殤王友卒。

translations.literal: In the second month, on bingzi, You, Prince of Shaoling, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on bingzi, the Prince of Shaoling, You, died.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，魏太皇太后及魏主如代郡溫泉。

translations.literal: On xinsi, the Wei Grand Empress Dowager and the Wei emperor went to the hot springs in Dai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, the Northern Wei empress dowager and emperor visited the hot springs in Dai.

sentences.zh: 甲午，詔申前命，命太傅贊拜不名。

translations.literal: On jiawu, an edict reaffirmed the earlier order: the Grand Tutor, when assisting at audiences, was not to have his name called.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, an edict renewed a prior privilege: at court the Grand Tutor was to be announced without his personal name being spoken.

sentences.zh: 己亥，魏太皇太后及魏主如西宮。

translations.literal: On jihai, the Wei Grand Empress Dowager and the Wei emperor went to the Western Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, the Wei empress dowager and emperor went to the Western Palace.

sentences.zh: 三月，癸卯朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the first day guimao, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the third month there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以太傅爲相國，總百揆，封十郡，爲齊公，加九錫；

translations.literal: On jiachen, the Grand Tutor was made Chancellor of State, overseeing all government, enfeoffed with ten commanderies as Duke of Qi, and granted the Nine Bestowals;
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, the Grand Tutor was made chancellor, given charge of all affairs, enfeoffed as Duke of Qi over ten commanderies, and granted the Nine Bestowals;

sentences.zh: 其驃騎大將軍、揚州牧、南徐州刺史如故。

translations.literal: his posts as General of Agile Cavalry, Governor of Yangzhou, and Inspector of South Xuzhou remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: while he retained his titles as General of Agile Cavalry, governor of Yangzhou, and inspector of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，詔齊國官爵禮儀，並仿天朝。

translations.literal: On yisi, an edict ordered that the offices, ranks, and rituals of the state of Qi were all to follow the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, an edict declared that Qi's offices, ranks, and ceremonies were to mirror those of the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以世子賾領南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the heir Ze was put in charge of South Yuzhou as Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, the heir Ze was made acting inspector of South Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 楊運長去宜城郡還家，齊公遣人殺之。

translations.literal: Yang Yunchang, having left Yicheng Commandery and returned home, was killed by men sent by the Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yunchang, who had left his post in Yicheng and gone home, was assassinated on the Duke of Qi's orders.

sentences.zh: 凌源令潘智與運長厚善；

translations.literal: Pan Zhi, magistrate of Lingyuan, was on close terms with Yunchang;
translations.idiomatic: Pan Zhi, magistrate of Lingyuan, had been a close friend of Yunchang;

sentences.zh: 臨川王綽，義慶之孫也。

translations.literal: Prince Chuo of Linchuan was a grandson of Liu Yiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chuo of Linchuan was a grandson of Liu Yiqing.

sentences.zh: 綽遣腹心陳言贊説智曰：「君先帝舊人，身是宗室近屬，如此形勢，豈得久全！

translations.literal: Chuo sent a trusted man, Chen, to praise and persuade Zhi, saying: "You are an old retainer of the former emperor and yourself a close kinsman of the imperial clan — in such a situation, how can you long remain safe!
translations.idiomatic: Chuo sent a confidant named Chen to flatter and win over Zhi: "You served the late emperor and are near kin to the house of Liu — in the present situation, how can you hope to survive?

sentences.zh: 若招合內外，計多有從者。

translations.literal: If you rally inside and outside the capital, I reckon many will follow.
translations.idiomatic: Rally supporters inside and outside the palace, and many will join you.

sentences.zh: 台城內人常有此心，正苦無人建意耳！」

translations.literal: People within the capital often harbor this mind; they only suffer from having no one to raise the plan!"
translations.idiomatic: Many inside the capital already feel the same — they only lack someone to lead them!"

sentences.zh: 智即以告齊公。

translations.literal: Zhi at once reported this to the Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi immediately informed the Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，誅綽兄弟及共黨與。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Chuo, his brothers, and their fellow conspirators were executed.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Chuo, his brothers, and their accomplices were put to death.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，齊公受策命，赦其境內，以石頭爲世子宮，一如東宮。

translations.literal: On jiayin, the Duke of Qi received the investiture mandate, amnestied his domain, and made Stone City the heir's palace, just like the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, the Duke of Qi accepted the formal mandate, pardoned his territories, and established Stone City as the crown prince's residence, matching the imperial Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 褚淵引何曾自魏司徒爲晉丞相故事，求爲齊官，齊公不許。

translations.literal: Chu Yuan cited the precedent of He Zeng, who went from Wei Minister of Works to Jin Chancellor, and asked to serve as an official of Qi; the Duke of Qi did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan cited He Zeng's move from Wei minister to Jin chancellor and asked to take office under Qi; the duke refused.

sentences.zh: 以王儉爲齊尚書右僕射，領吏部；

translations.literal: Wang Jian was made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat of Qi, overseeing the Ministry of Personnel;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian was appointed Right Vice Director of Qi's Secretariat and head of the Ministry of Personnel;

sentences.zh: 儉時年二十八。

translations.literal: Jian was then twenty-eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was only twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，武陵王贊卒，非疾也。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Zan, Prince of Wuling, died — not of illness.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, the Prince of Wuling, Zan, died — not of natural causes.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，加齊王殊禮，進世子爲太子。

translations.literal: On bingxu, extraordinary honors were added for the King of Qi, and the heir was advanced to Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, the King of Qi was granted extraordinary honors, and his heir was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，宋順帝下詔禪位於齊。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Emperor Shun of Song issued an edict abdicating the throne to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Emperor Shun of Liu Song issued an edict abdicating in favor of Qi.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，帝當臨軒，不肯出，逃於佛蓋之下，王敬則勒兵殿庭，以板輿入迎帝。

translations.literal: On renchen, the emperor was to appear at the audience hall but would not come out; he fled beneath the Buddha canopy. Wang Jingze arrayed troops in the palace courtyard and sent in a litter to fetch the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, when the emperor was due to take the throne for the abdication, he refused to appear and hid under a Buddhist canopy. Wang Jingze drew up troops in the courtyard and sent a palanquin to bring him out.

sentences.zh: 太后懼，自帥閹人索得之，敬則啟譬令出，引令升車。

translations.literal: The empress dowager, in fear, herself led eunuchs to search him out; Jingze admonished and persuaded him to come out and helped him into the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The terrified empress dowager led eunuchs to find him; Jingze coaxed him out and helped him into the litter.

sentences.zh: 帝收淚謂敬則曰：「欲見殺乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor wiped his tears and said to Jingze: "Do you mean to have me killed?"
translations.idiomatic: Wiping his tears, the boy emperor asked Jingze, "Are you going to kill me?"

sentences.zh: 敬則曰：「出居別宮耳。

translations.literal: Jingze said: "You are only to go live in a separate palace.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze replied, "You are only being moved to another palace.

sentences.zh: 官先取司馬家亦如此。」

translations.literal: Our office took the Sima family the same way before."
translations.idiomatic: We did the same with the Sima family."

sentences.zh: 帝泣而彈指曰：「願後身世世勿復生天王家！」

translations.literal: The emperor wept and snapped his fingers, saying: "May I never again be born into an imperial clan in any later life!"
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, the emperor snapped his fingers and cried, "May I never be born into an emperor's house again!"

sentences.zh: 宮中皆哭。

translations.literal: Everyone in the palace wept.
translations.idiomatic: The whole palace wept with him.

sentences.zh: 帝拍敬則手曰：「必無過慮，當餉輔國十萬錢。」

translations.literal: The emperor patted Jingze's hand and said: "You need not worry excessively; I shall reward the Defender of the State one hundred thousand cash."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor patted Jingze's hand and said, "Do not worry — I will give you a hundred thousand cash as Defender of the State."

sentences.zh: 是日，百僚陪位。

translations.literal: That day, the hundred officials took their places in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: That day the officials took their places for the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 侍中謝朏在直，當解璽綬，陽爲不知，曰：「有何公事？」

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Xie Tiao was on duty and was to remove the imperial seal and cord; he feigned ignorance and said: "What official business is there?"
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Xie Tiao, on duty to receive the imperial seal, pretended not to understand and asked, "What business brings you?"

sentences.zh: 傳詔云：「解璽綬授齊王。」

translations.literal: The edict-bearer said: "Remove the seal and cord and hand them to the King of Qi."
translations.idiomatic: The messenger said, "Remove the seal and cord and give them to the King of Qi."

sentences.zh: 朏曰：「齊自應有侍中。」

translations.literal: Tiao said: "Qi ought to have its own Palace Attendant."
translations.idiomatic: Tiao answered, "Qi should have its own palace attendant for that."

sentences.zh: 乃引枕臥。

translations.literal: He then pulled a pillow and lay down.
translations.idiomatic: He pulled over a pillow and lay down.

sentences.zh: 傳詔懼，使朏稱疾，欲取兼人，朏曰：「我無疾，何所道！」

translations.literal: The edict-bearer was afraid and had Tiao claim illness, wishing to find a substitute; Tiao said: "I am not ill — what is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, the messenger urged Tiao to plead illness and find a substitute; Tiao said, "I am not ill — what excuse should I give?"

sentences.zh: 遂朝服步出東掖門，仍登車還宅。

translations.literal: He then went out in court dress on foot through the Eastern Side Gate, mounted his carriage, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He walked out through the Eastern Side Gate in full court dress, boarded his carriage, and went home.

sentences.zh: 乃以王儉爲侍中，解璽綬。

translations.literal: Wang Jian was then made Palace Attendant and removed the seal and cord.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian was appointed Palace Attendant and took the seal and cord instead.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，帝乘畫輪車，出東掖門就東邸，問：「今日何不奏鼓吹？」

translations.literal: When the rites were finished, the emperor rode a painted-wheeled carriage, went out the Eastern Side Gate to the Eastern Residence, and asked: "Why is no music played today?"
translations.idiomatic: After the ceremony the emperor rode out through the Eastern Side Gate to his eastern residence and asked, "Why is there no ceremonial music today?"

sentences.zh: 左右莫有應者。

translations.literal: None of those beside him answered.
translations.idiomatic: No one beside him answered.

sentences.zh: 右光祿大夫王琨，華之從父弟也，在晉世已爲郎中，至是，攀車獺尾慟哭曰：「人以壽爲歡，老臣以壽爲戚。

translations.literal: Wang Kun, Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and younger cousin of Wang Hua, had already been a Gentleman in the Jin era; on this occasion he clutched the otter-tail ornament on the carriage and wailed: "Others take long life for joy; this old minister takes long life for sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kun, Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and a cousin of Wang Hua, had served as a court gentleman under Jin; now he seized the otter-tail fringe on the imperial carriage and sobbed, "Others rejoice in long life — I grieve in it.

sentences.zh: 既不能先驅螻蟻，乃復頻見此事！」

translations.literal: Having failed to go ahead as a pioneer among the ants, I must yet again often witness this affair!"
translations.idiomatic: I could not die before my sovereign, and now I must witness this again and again!"

sentences.zh: 嗚咽不自勝，百官雨泣。

translations.literal: He sobbed beyond control; the hundred officials wept like rain.
translations.idiomatic: He could not stop weeping, and the officials wept with him like rain.

sentences.zh: 司空兼太保褚淵等奉璽綬，帥百官詣齊宮勸進；

translations.literal: Minister of Works and concurrent Grand Tutor Chu Yuan and others bore the seal and cord, led the hundred officials to the Qi palace to urge acceptance of the throne;
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan, Minister of Works and Grand Tutor, and others carried the seal and cord and led the officials to the Qi palace to urge the duke to accept the throne;

sentences.zh: 王辭讓未受。

translations.literal: the king declined and did not yet accept.
translations.idiomatic: but he declined and would not yet accept.

sentences.zh: 淵從弟前安成太守炤謂淵子賁曰：「司空今日何在？」

translations.literal: Yuan's younger cousin Chu Zhao, former Administrator of Ancheng, said to Yuan's son Ben: "Where is the Minister of Works today?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's cousin Chu Zhao, former administrator of Ancheng, asked Yuan's son Ben, "Where is the Minister of Works today?"

sentences.zh: 賁曰：「奉璽綬在齊大司馬門。」

translations.literal: Ben said: "Bearing the seal and cord at the Great Marshal's gate of Qi."
translations.idiomatic: Ben replied, "Presenting the seal and cord at the Great Marshal's gate of Qi."

sentences.zh: □召曰：「不知汝家司空將一家物與一家，亦復何謂！」

translations.literal: Zhao said: "I do not understand your family's Minister of Works handing the possessions of one house to another house — what is that supposed to mean!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "So your family's Minister of Works is handing one dynasty's possessions to another — what sort of conduct is that?"

sentences.zh: 甲午，王即皇帝位於南郊。

translations.literal: On jiawu, the king took the imperial position at the Southern Altar.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, he ascended the throne at the Southern Altar.

sentences.zh: 還宮，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: Returning to the palace, he proclaimed a great amnesty and changed the reign title.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the palace, he proclaimed a general amnesty and adopted a new reign title.

sentences.zh: 奉宋順帝爲汝陰王，優崇之禮，皆仿宋初。

translations.literal: He honored Emperor Shun of Song as Prince of Ruyin; the preferential honors all followed the pattern of the early Song.
translations.idiomatic: He ennobled Emperor Shun as Prince of Ruyin with honors modeled on those Song had granted the deposed Jin emperor.

sentences.zh: 築宮丹楊，置兵守衛之。

translations.literal: A palace was built in Danyang and troops were posted to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: A residence was built for him in Danyang and garrisoned with troops.

sentences.zh: 宋神主遷汝陰廟，諸王皆降爲公；

translations.literal: The Song imperial ancestral tablets were moved to the Ruyin temple; all princes were demoted to dukes;
translations.idiomatic: The Song imperial ancestral tablets were moved to the Ruyin shrine, and all princes were reduced to dukes;

sentences.zh: 自非宣力齊室，餘皆除國，獨置南康、華容、萍鄉三國，以奉劉穆之、王弘、何無忌之後，除國者凡百二十人。

translations.literal: except those who had declared their service to the house of Qi, the rest all had their states abolished; only the three states of Nankang, Huarong, and Pingxiang were retained to support the descendants of Liu Muzhi, Wang Hong, and He Wuji — those deprived of states numbered one hundred twenty in all.
translations.idiomatic: and except for men who had openly served Qi, every other fief was abolished. Only the states of Nankang, Huarong, and Pingxiang were kept, for the descendants of Liu Muzhi, Wang Hong, and He Wuji; one hundred twenty men lost their fiefs altogether.

sentences.zh: 二台官僚，依任攝職，名號不同、員限盈長者，別更詳議。

translations.literal: The officials of the two secretariats continued in their provisional posts according to appointment; where titles differed or establishment limits were excessive, these were to be reconsidered in detail separately.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the two secretariats kept their provisional posts for the time being; titles that no longer matched or establishments that had grown too large were to be reviewed separately.

sentences.zh: 以褚淵爲司徒。

translations.literal: Chu Yuan was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 賓客賀者滿座，褚炤歎曰：「彥回少立名行，何意披猖至此！

translations.literal: Guests offering congratulations filled the seats; Chu Zhao sighed and said: "Yanhui in his youth established name and conduct — who would have thought he would run riot to this point!
translations.idiomatic: When congratulatory guests filled the hall, Chu Zhao sighed, "Yanhui built his reputation young — who would have thought he would come to this!

sentences.zh: 門戶不幸，乃復有今日之拜。

translations.literal: Our house is unfortunate — and now this appointment of today.
translations.idiomatic: Our family is ill-fated to see this appointment today.

sentences.zh: 使彥回作中書郎而死，不當爲一名士邪！

translations.literal: If Yanhui had served as a Secretariat Gentleman and then died, would he not have been a famous gentleman!
translations.idiomatic: Had Yanhui died as a Secretariat Gentleman, would he not have been remembered as a gentleman of note?

sentences.zh: 名德不昌，用復有期頤之壽！」

translations.literal: His fame and virtue did not flourish — yet he still lives to a full hundred!"
translations.idiomatic: His fame never flourished, yet he lives on to a ripe old age!"

sentences.zh: 淵固辭不拜。

translations.literal: Yuan firmly declined and did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan firmly refused the post.

sentences.zh: 奉朝請河東裴覬上表，數帝過惡，掛冠徑去；

translations.literal: Pei Gui of Hedong, a Court Attendant, submitted a memorial enumerating the emperor's faults and offenses, hung up his cap and left directly;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Gui of Hedong, a court attendant, submitted a memorial listing the emperor's crimes, resigned his office, and left;

sentences.zh: 帝怒，殺之。

translations.literal: the emperor was angry and had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor had him executed in anger.

sentences.zh: 太子賾請殺謝朏，帝曰：「殺之遂成其名，正應容之度外耳。」

translations.literal: Crown Prince Ze asked to kill Xie Tiao; the emperor said: "Killing him would only make his name — we should simply tolerate him beyond measure."
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Ze asked that Xie Tiao be killed; the emperor said, "To kill him would only glorify him — better to ignore him entirely."

sentences.zh: 久之，因事廢於家。

translations.literal: After a long while, on some pretext he was dismissed and kept at home.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually, on another charge, Tiao was dismissed and confined at home.

sentences.zh: 帝問爲政於前撫軍行參軍沛國劉□獻，對曰：「政在《孝經》。

translations.literal: The emperor asked about governing from Liu Xian of Pei, former Staff Officer on the March of the Pacifying Army, who answered: "Government lies in the Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Liu Xian of Pei, formerly a staff officer on the Pacifying Army staff, about government; he answered, "Government lies in the Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 凡宋氏所以亡，陛下所以得者，皆是也。

translations.literal: All that caused the house of Song to perish and Your Majesty to gain the throne is contained in it.
translations.idiomatic: Everything that destroyed Song and brought Your Majesty to power is there.

sentences.zh: 陛下若戒前車之失，加之以寬厚，雖危可安；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty takes warning from the overturned cart ahead and adds leniency and generosity, though in peril you may be made secure;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty learns from the fallen cart ahead and rules with leniency, even danger can be made safe;

sentences.zh: 若循其覆轍，雖安必危矣！」

translations.literal: if you follow their overturned track, though secure you will surely be in peril!"
translations.idiomatic: but if you follow their tracks, even security will end in peril!"

sentences.zh: 帝歎曰：「儒者之言，可寶萬世！」

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said: "The words of the Confucians may be treasured for ten thousand generations!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed and said, "A Confucian's words are a treasure for ten thousand generations!"

translations.literal: Closing quotation.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation.

sentences.zh: 丙申，魏主如崞山。

translations.literal: On bingshen, the Wei emperor went to Mount Guo.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, the Northern Wei emperor went to Mount Guo.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以太子詹事張緒爲中書令，齊國左衛將軍陳顯達爲中護軍，右衛將軍李安民爲中領軍。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Zhang Xu, Steward of the Crown Prince's Household, was made Director of the Secretariat; Chen Xianda, Left Guard General of Qi, was made General Protecting the Army; Li Anmin, Right Guard General, was made General Commanding the Army.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Zhang Xu became Director of the Secretariat; Chen Xianda, Qi's Left Guard General, became General Protecting the Army; and Li Anmin, Right Guard General, became General Commanding the Army.

sentences.zh: 緒，岱之兄子也。

translations.literal: Xu was a nephew of Zhang Dai on his elder brother's side.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was a nephew of Zhang Dai.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以荊州刺史嶷爲尚書令、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Yan, Governor of Jingzhou, was made Director of the Secretariat, General of Agile Cavalry, Director with protocols equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Xiao Yan was made Director of the Secretariat, General of Agile Cavalry with an office equal to the Three Excellencies, and governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝命群臣各言得失。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the ministers each to speak of what was right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his ministers each to speak on the strengths and failings of government.

sentences.zh: 淮南、宣城二郡太守劉善明，請除宋氏大明、泰始以來諸苛政細制，以崇簡易。

translations.literal: Liu Shanming, Administrator of the two commanderies Huainan and Xuancheng, asked to abolish the harsh policies and minute regulations since the Daming and Taishi eras of Song, to promote simplicity and ease.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shanming, administrator of Huainan and Xuancheng, urged abolition of the harsh laws and petty regulations dating from Emperor Xiaowu's and Emperor Ming's reigns, in favor of simpler government.

sentences.zh: 又以爲：「交州險遠，宋末政苛，遂至怨叛。

translations.literal: He also held: "Jiaozhou is perilous and remote; at the end of Song government was harsh, until resentment led to rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued, "Jiaozhou is remote and difficult; under the late Song its harsh rule provoked rebellion.

sentences.zh: 今大化創始，宜懷以恩德。

translations.literal: Now that great transformation is newly begun, it is fitting to embrace them with grace and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: With a new dynasty just begun, they should be won over with kindness.

sentences.zh: 且彼土所出，唯有珠寶，實非聖朝所須之急。

translations.literal: Moreover, what that land produces is only pearls and jewels — truly not an urgent need of the sage court.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, that region yields only pearls and jewels — nothing the court urgently needs.

sentences.zh: 討伐之事，謂宜且停。」

translations.literal: Campaigns of suppression, I hold, should for the present be halted."
translations.idiomatic: Military expeditions there should be suspended for now."

sentences.zh: 給事黃門郎清河崔祖思亦上言，以爲：「人不學則不知道，此悖逆禍亂所由生也。

translations.literal: Cui Zusi of Qinghe, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate in the Secretariat Service, also submitted a memorial, holding: "If people do not study, they do not know the Way — this is what gives rise to rebellion and calamitous disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zusi of Qinghe, an Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, also memorialized the throne: "Without learning, people do not know the Way — and from that come rebellion and disorder.

sentences.zh: 今無員之官，空受祿秩，凋耗民財。

translations.literal: Today officials without established posts vainly receive salaries and ranks, draining the people's wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Today supernumerary officials draw salaries without posts, draining the people's wealth.

sentences.zh: 宜開文武二學，課台、府、州、國限外之人各從所樂，依方習業，若有廢惰者，遣還故郡；

translations.literal: It is fitting to open civil and military schools, assign men beyond the quotas of the Secretariat, prefectures, provinces, and princedoms each to follow his inclination, study his specialty according to his bent; if any are idle and lazy, send them back to their native commanderies;
translations.idiomatic: Establish civil and military schools, enroll men beyond the regular quotas from the capital, prefectures, provinces, and princedoms to study as they choose, and send the idle back to their home districts;

sentences.zh: 經藝優殊者，待以不次。

translations.literal: those outstanding in the classics and arts should be advanced out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: those who excel in the classics should be promoted without regard to seniority.

sentences.zh: 又，今陛下雖履節儉，而群下猶安習侈靡。

translations.literal: Moreover, though Your Majesty now practices frugality, your subordinates still rest content in accustomed luxury.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though Your Majesty practices frugality, your officials still cling to lavish habits.

sentences.zh: 宜褒進朝士之約素清修者，貶退其驕奢荒淫者，則風俗可移矣。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to praise and advance court gentlemen who are plain and pure in conduct, and demote those who are arrogant, extravagant, and dissolute — then customs may be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Reward plain, upright courtiers and demote the arrogant and dissolute, and customs will change."

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉之世，凡事皆責成郡縣。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era of Song, all affairs were charged to the commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen of Song, every task was entrusted to the local commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 世祖徵求急速，以郡縣遲緩，始遣台使督之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu made levies urgent; because commanderies and counties were slow, he first sent capital inspectors to supervise them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu demanded rapid collection; when the localities lagged, he began sending capital inspectors to supervise them.

sentences.zh: 自是使者所在旁午，競作威福，營私納賂，公私勞擾。

translations.literal: From then on inspectors were everywhere in succession, each vying to wield power and favor, seeking private gain and taking bribes, to the weariness of public and private alike.
translations.idiomatic: From then on capital envoys swarmed everywhere, abusing their power, taking bribes, and exhausting both government and people.

sentences.zh: 會稽太守聞喜公子良上表極陳其弊，以爲：「台有求須，但明下詔敕，爲之期會，則人思自竭；

translations.literal: Xiao Ziliang, Administrator of Kuaiji and son of the Prince of Wenxi, submitted a memorial setting forth these abuses in full, holding: "When the capital has requirements, it need only issue clear edicts and set deadlines — then people will strive of themselves to exhaust their efforts;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ziliang, administrator of Kuaiji, memorialized at length against the abuse, arguing, "When the court needs something, it should issue clear orders with deadlines — then people will exert themselves;

sentences.zh: 若有稽遲，自依糾坐之科。

translations.literal: if there is delay, let the statutes on investigation and punishment apply of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: if there is delay, let the regular penalties apply.

sentences.zh: 今雖台使盈湊，會取正屬所辦，徒相疑憤，反更淹懈，宜悉停台使。」

translations.literal: Now though capital inspectors crowd in, in the end they take what the responsible officials have done — only mutual suspicion and resentment result, and slackness grows worse; capital inspectors should all be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: Today, though envoys crowd in, they ultimately rely on what local officials have done — breeding only suspicion and delay. All such envoys should be abolished."

sentences.zh: 員外散騎郎劉思效上言：「宋自大明以來，漸見凋弊，徵賦有加而天府尤貧。

translations.literal: Liu Sixiao, Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant, also submitted a memorial: "Since the Daming era, Song has gradually declined; levies have increased while the imperial treasury has grown especially poor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sixiao, a supernumerary cavalier attendant, also memorialized: "Since the Daming era, the dynasty has declined; taxes have risen while the treasury has grown poorer still.

sentences.zh: 小民嗷嗷，殆無生意；

translations.literal: The common people cry out in distress, scarcely with any will to live;
translations.idiomatic: The common people cry out in misery, barely able to survive;

sentences.zh: 而貴族富室，以侈麗相高，乃至山澤之民，不敢採食其水草。

translations.literal: yet the noble and wealthy vie with one another in splendor, until even people of the hills and marshes dare not gather and eat the plants and fish of the waters.
translations.idiomatic: while the rich compete in luxury, until even mountain folk dare not gather wild plants or fish from the streams.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜一新王度，革正其失。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should renew the royal norms and correct these errors."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should renew the norms of kingship and correct these abuses."

sentences.zh: 上皆加褒賞，或以表付外，使有司詳擇所宜，奏行之。

translations.literal: The emperor in each case added praise and reward, or handed the memorial outside for the relevant offices to choose in detail what was fitting and memorialize for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and rewarded each man, and referred some memorials to the ministries to select what was suitable and put into practice.

sentences.zh: 己亥，詔：「二宮諸王，悉不得營立屯邸，封略山湖。」

translations.literal: On jihai, an edict: "Princes of the two palaces and all other princes are forbidden to establish estates and manors or to seize and enclose mountains and lakes."
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, an edict declared that princes of both palaces and all other princes were forbidden to build private estates or seize mountains and lakes.

translations.literal: Closing quotation.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation.

sentences.zh: 魏主還平城。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 魏秦州刺史尉洛侯、雍州刺史宜都王目辰、長安鎮將陳提等皆坐貪殘不法，洛侯、目辰伏誅，提徙邊。

translations.literal: Wei Governor of Qinzhou Wei Luohou, Governor of Yongzhou Prince Muchen of Yidu, and Garrison General of Chang'an Chen Ti were all convicted of greedy cruelty and lawlessness; Luohou and Muchen were executed, Ti was banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei governors Wei Luohou of Qinzhou and Prince Muchen of Yidu, and the Chang'an garrison commander Chen Ti, were all convicted of corruption and cruelty; Luohou and Muchen were executed, and Ti was exiled.

sentences.zh: 又詔以「候官千數，重罪受賕不列，輕罪吹毛髮舉，宜悉罷之。」

translations.literal: Another edict held: "The inspector officials number in the thousands — on grave crimes they take bribes and do not report them, on light crimes they raise charges over the slightest hair — they should all be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict declared that the thousands of secret police who ignored major crimes for bribes yet prosecuted trivial offenses should all be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 更置謹直者數百人，使防邏街衢，執喧斗而已。

translations.literal: Several hundred upright and careful men were appointed in their place, to patrol the streets and handle brawls only.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred honest patrolmen were appointed instead, to guard the streets and deal only with brawls.

sentences.zh: 自是吏民始得安業。

translations.literal: From then on officials and people were at last able to pursue their occupations in peace.
translations.idiomatic: From then on officials and commoners could live in peace.

sentences.zh: 自泰始以來，內外多虞，將帥各募部曲，屯聚建康。

translations.literal: Since the Taishi era, there have been many troubles within and without; generals each recruited personal followings, massed at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Taishi era, turmoil at home and abroad had led every general to recruit private troops and concentrate them at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 李安民上表，以爲：「自非淮北常備外，餘軍悉皆輸遣；

translations.literal: Li Anmin submitted a memorial, holding: "Except for the standing forces north of the Huai, all other armies should be sent away;
translations.idiomatic: Li Anmin memorialized that except for the standing army north of the Huai, all other troops should be sent home;

sentences.zh: 若親近宜立隨身者，聽限人數。」

translations.literal: if close attendants require personal guards, let the number be limited."
translations.idiomatic: and if commanders needed personal guards, their numbers should be strictly limited.

sentences.zh: 上從之；

translations.literal: The emperor followed this;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed;

sentences.zh: 五月，辛亥，詔斷眾募。

translations.literal: in the fifth month, on xinhai, an edict ended mass recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: and in the fifth month, on xinhai, he forbade private recruitment.

sentences.zh: 壬子，上賞佐命之功，褚淵、王儉等進增爵、戶各有差。

translations.literal: On renzi, the emperor rewarded those who had aided in establishing the mandate; Chu Yuan, Wang Jian, and others were advanced in noble rank and household quotas, each according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, the emperor rewarded those who had helped him seize power; Chu Yuan, Wang Jian, and others received increased ranks and fiefs according to their merit.

sentences.zh: 處士何點謂人曰：「我作《齊書》已竟，贊云：『淵既世族，儉亦國華；

translations.literal: The recluse He Dian said to others: "I have finished my Book of Qi; the encomium reads: 'Yuan is already of an eminent clan, Jian also a flower of the state;
translations.idiomatic: The recluse He Dian remarked, "I have finished my Book of Qi; its encomium runs: 'Yuan is of a great clan, Jian a jewel of the state;

sentences.zh: 不賴舅氏，遑恤國家！』

translations.literal: not relying on maternal uncles — how could they spare a thought for the state!'
translations.idiomatic: relying not on their own merit but on their imperial in-laws — how could they care for the realm!'

sentences.zh: 」點，尚之之孫也。

translations.literal: Dian was a grandson of He Shangzhi.'
translations.idiomatic: Dian was a grandson of He Shangzhi.'

sentences.zh: 淵母宋始安公主，繼母吳郡公主；

translations.literal: Yuan's mother was the Princess of Shian of Song; his stepmother was the Princess of Wu Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's mother had been the Princess of Shian; his stepmother was the Princess of Wu;

sentences.zh: 又尚巴西公主。

translations.literal: he also married the Princess of Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: and he himself married the Princess of Baxi.

sentences.zh: 儉母武康公主；

translations.literal: Jian's mother was the Princess of Wukang;
translations.idiomatic: Jian's mother was the Princess of Wukang;

sentences.zh: 又尚陽羨公主。

translations.literal: he also married the Princess of Yangxian.
translations.idiomatic: and he married the Princess of Yangxian.

sentences.zh: 故點云然。

translations.literal: Therefore Dian spoke thus.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Dian's remark.

sentences.zh: 己未，或走馬過汝陰王之門，衛士恐有爲亂者奔入殺王，而以疾聞，上不罪而賞之。

translations.literal: On jiwei, someone galloped past the gate of the Prince of Ruyin; the guards, fearing a disturbance, rushed in and killed the prince, reporting it as illness — the emperor did not punish them but rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, a horseman rode past the Prince of Ruyin's gate; the guards, fearing a plot, rushed in and killed the deposed emperor, reporting that he had died of illness. The emperor not only spared them but rewarded them.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，殺宋宗室陰安公燮等，無少長皆死。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Xie and others of the Song imperial clan, including the Duke of Yin'an, were killed — none young or old was spared.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, the Liu princes including the Duke of Yin'an, Xie, were slaughtered to the last man, young and old alike.

sentences.zh: 前豫州刺史劉澄之，遵考之子也，與褚淵善，淵爲之固請曰：「澄之兄弟不武，且於劉宗又疏。」

translations.literal: Former Inspector of Yuzhou Liu Chengzhi, son of Liu Zunkao, was on good terms with Chu Yuan; Yuan pleaded firmly for him, saying: "Chengzhi and his brothers are not martial, and are moreover remote from the Liu clan."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chengzhi, former inspector of Yuzhou and son of Liu Zunkao, was a friend of Chu Yuan, who pleaded for him: "Chengzhi and his brothers are not warriors and are only distantly related to the Liu house."

sentences.zh: 故遵考之族獨得免。

translations.literal: Therefore Zunkao's clan alone was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zunkao's branch of the family was spared.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，追尊皇考曰宣皇帝，皇妣陳氏曰孝皇后。

translations.literal: On bingyin, the emperor's late father was posthumously honored as Emperor Xuan, and his late mother, Lady Chen, as Empress Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, the emperor posthumously honored his father as Emperor Xuan and his mother, Lady Chen, as Empress Xiao.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，封皇子鈞爲衡陽王。

translations.literal: On dingmao, the imperial son Jun was enfeoffed as Prince of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, the prince Jun was enfeoffed as Prince of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 上謂兗州刺史垣崇祖曰：「吾新得天下，索虜必以納劉昶爲辭，侵犯邊鄙。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Yuan Chongzu, Inspector of Yanzhou: "I have newly gained the realm; the northern barbarians will surely use their reception of Liu Chang as a pretext to invade the borders.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Yuan Chongzu, inspector of Yanzhou, "I have only just taken the throne; the northerners will surely use their sheltering of Liu Chang as a pretext to raid the frontier.

sentences.zh: 壽陽當虜之沖，非卿無以制此虜也。」

translations.literal: Shouyang lies in the path of the barbarians — without you there is no one to check them."
translations.idiomatic: Shouyang lies in their path — only you can hold them back."

sentences.zh: 乃徙崇祖爲豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Chongzu was then transferred to be Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He transferred Chongzu to Yuzhou as inspector.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙子，誅游擊將軍姚道和，以其貳於沈攸之也。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on bingzi, Mobile General Yao Daohe was executed for having sided with Shen Youzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingzi, Mobile General Yao Daohe was executed for having sided with Shen Youzhi.

sentences.zh: 甲子，立太子賾爲皇太子；

translations.literal: On jiazi, Crown Prince Ze was established as Imperial Heir;
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Ze was formally invested as crown prince;

sentences.zh: 皇子嶷爲豫章王，映爲臨川王，暠爲安成王，鏘爲鄱陽王，鑠爲桂陽王，鑒爲廣陵王；

translations.literal: the imperial sons Yan as Prince of Yuzhang, Ying as Prince of Linchuan, Gao as Prince of Ancheng, Qiang as Prince of Poyang, Shuo as Prince of Guiyang, and Jian as Prince of Guangling;
translations.idiomatic: and his sons Yan, Ying, Gao, Qiang, Shuo, and Jian were made princes of Yuzhang, Linchuan, Ancheng, Poyang, Guiyang, and Guangling;

sentences.zh: 皇孫長懋爲南郡王。

translations.literal: the imperial grandson Changmao as Prince of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: while his grandson Changmao was made Prince of Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，葬宋順帝於遂寧陵。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Emperor Shun of Song was buried at Suining Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, the deposed Emperor Shun of Song was buried at Suining Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 帝以建康居民舛雜，多奸盜，欲立符伍以相檢括，右僕射王儉諫曰：「京師之地，四方輻湊，必也持符，於事既煩，理成不曠；

translations.literal: The emperor, because the residents of Jiankang were mixed and disorderly and there were many thieves, wished to establish household registers and mutual responsibility for inspection. Wang Jian, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, remonstrated: "The capital is where the four quarters converge — if passes must be shown, affairs become burdensome and reason itself cannot be broad;
translations.idiomatic: Because Jiankang's population was mixed and crime rampant, the emperor wished to impose household registration and mutual surveillance. Wang Jian, Right Vice Director, objected: "The capital draws people from every quarter — requiring passes at every turn would burden everyone and defeat its own purpose;

sentences.zh: 謝安所謂『不爾何以爲京師』也。」

translations.literal: it is what Xie An meant by 'if it were not so, how could it be the capital.'"
translations.idiomatic: as Xie An said, 'if it were not so, how could it be the capital.'"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The plan was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 初，交州刺史李長仁卒，從弟叔獻代領州事，以號令未行，遣使求刺史於宋。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Changren, Inspector of Jiaozhou, died; his younger cousin Shuxian took charge of the province in his stead. Because his orders did not prevail, he sent envoys to request an inspector from Song.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Changren, inspector of Jiaozhou, died, his cousin Shuxian took over the province but, lacking imperial authority, asked Song to appoint a governor.

sentences.zh: 宋以南海太守沈煥爲交州刺史，以叔獻爲煥寧遠司馬、武平、新昌二郡太守。

translations.literal: Song appointed Shen Huan, Administrator of Nanhai, Inspector of Jiaozhou, and made Shuxian Huan's Pacification of the Distance Staff Officer and Administrator of the two commanderies Wuping and Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: Song named Shen Huan of Nanhai inspector of Jiaozhou and made Shuxian his deputy with command over Wuping and Xinchang.

sentences.zh: 叔獻既得朝命，人情服從，遂發兵守險，不納煥。

translations.literal: Once Shuxian had the court appointment, popular sentiment submitted; he then raised troops to hold the passes and would not admit Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shuxian held the court's commission, he won local support, garrisoned the passes, and refused to admit Huan.

sentences.zh: 煥停鬱林，病卒。

translations.literal: Huan halted at Yulin and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Huan halted at Yulin and died there of illness.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁未，詔曰：「交趾、比景獨隔書朔，斯乃前運方季，因迷遂往。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on dingwei, an edict said: "Jiaozhi and Bijing alone are cut off from our calendar — this is because the previous mandate was in its decline and they went astray.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the seventh month's dingwei day, an edict declared, "Jiaozhi and Bijing alone have been cut off from the court's calendar — a legacy of the previous dynasty's decline and their own confusion.

sentences.zh: 宜曲赦交州，即以叔獻爲刺史，撫安南土。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to grant a special amnesty in Jiaozhou, appoint Shuxian inspector at once, and pacify the southern lands."
translations.idiomatic: Grant a special amnesty in Jiaozhou, appoint Shuxian inspector, and pacify the south."

translations.literal: Closing quotation.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation.

sentences.zh: 魏葭蘆鎮主楊廣香請降，丙辰，以廣香爲沙州刺史。

translations.literal: Yang Guangxiang, commandant of Jialu Garrison in Wei, requested surrender; on bingchen he was made Governor of Shazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guangxiang, the Wei garrison commander at Jialu, surrendered; on bingchen he was made governor of Shazhou.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙亥，魏主如方山；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on yihai, the Wei emperor went to Mount Fang;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yihai, the Wei emperor visited Mount Fang;

sentences.zh: 丁丑，還宮。

translations.literal: on dingchou, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: and on dingchou returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 上聞魏將入寇，九月，乙巳，復以豫章王嶷爲荊、湘二州刺史，都督如故；

translations.literal: Hearing that Wei would invade, in the ninth month, on yisi, Prince Yan of Yuzhang was again made Inspector of Jing and Xiang provinces, with command as before;
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Wei would invade, in the ninth month, on yisi, the emperor again made Prince Yan of Yuzhang inspector of Jing and Xiang with his former command;

sentences.zh: 以臨川王映爲揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Prince Ying of Linchuan was made Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: and Prince Ying of Linchuan governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以司空褚淵領尚書令。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Minister of Works Chu Yuan was put in charge of the Secretariat as Director.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Chu Yuan, Minister of Works, was made acting Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 壬子，魏以侍中、司徒、東陽王丕爲太尉，侍中、尚書右僕射陳建爲司徒，侍中、尚書代人苟頹爲司空。

translations.literal: On renzi, Wei made Prince Pi of Dongyang, Palace Attendant and Minister of Works, Grand Marshal; Chen Jian, Palace Attendant and Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, Minister of Works; and Gou Tui of Dairen, Palace Attendant and Secretary, Minister of the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Wei appointed Prince Pi of Dongyang Grand Marshal, Chen Jian Minister of Works, and Gou Tui Minister of the Masses.

sentences.zh: 己未，魏安樂厲王長樂謀反，賜死。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Prince Changle of Anle in Wei plotted rebellion and was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Prince Changle of Anle plotted rebellion and was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 庚申，魏隴西宣王源賀卒。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Yuan He, Prince Xuan of Longxi in Wei, died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Yuan He, Prince Xuan of Longxi, died.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己巳朔，魏大赦。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day jisi, Wei proclaimed a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on the first day of the tenth month, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 癸未，汝陰太妃王氏卒，謚曰宋恭皇后。

translations.literal: On guiwei, the Dowager Consort Wang of Ruyin died; her posthumous title was Empress Gong of Song.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, the Dowager Consort Wang of Ruyin died and was posthumously titled Empress Gong of Song.

sentences.zh: 初，晉壽民李烏奴與白水氐楊成等寇梁州，梁州刺史范柏年説降烏奴，擊楊成等，破之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Wunu of Jinshou and Yang Cheng of the Baishui Di and others raided Liangzhou; Fan Bonian, Inspector of Liangzhou, persuaded Wunu to surrender, attacked Yang Cheng and the rest, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Wunu of Jinshou and the Di chieftain Yang Cheng had raided Liangzhou; Inspector Fan Bonian persuaded Wunu to submit and defeated Yang Cheng's forces.

sentences.zh: 及沈攸之事起，柏年遣兵出魏興，聲雲入援，實候望形勢。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair arose, Bonian sent troops out from Weixing, declaring he would enter to aid, but in fact he watched how matters stood.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, Bonian marched out of Weixing claiming to aid the court while in fact waiting to see which side would win.

sentences.zh: 事平，朝廷遣王玄邈代之。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, the court sent Wang Xuanmiao to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed, the court sent Wang Xuanmiao to replace him.

sentences.zh: 詔柏年與烏奴俱下，烏奴勸柏年不受代；

translations.literal: An edict ordered Bonian and Wunu both to come down; Wunu urged Bonian not to accept replacement;
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Bonian and Wunu to leave the region; Wunu urged Bonian to refuse replacement;

sentences.zh: 柏年計未決，玄邈已至。

translations.literal: Bonian had not yet decided when Xuanmiao had already arrived.
translations.idiomatic: but before Bonian could decide, Xuanmiao had already arrived.

sentences.zh: 柏年乃留烏奴於漢中，還至魏興，盤桓不進。

translations.literal: Bonian then left Wunu at Hanzhong, returned to Weixing, and lingered without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Bonian left Wunu at Hanzhong, returned to Weixing, and lingered without proceeding to the capital.

sentences.zh: 左衛率豫章胡諧之嘗就柏年求馬，柏年曰：「馬非狗也，安能應無已之求！」

translations.literal: Hu Xiezhi of Yuzhang, Leader of the Left Guard, once went to Bonian to request horses; Bonian said: "Horses are not dogs — how can they answer endless demands!"
translations.idiomatic: Hu Xiezhi of the Left Guard once asked Bonian for horses; Bonian refused: "Horses are not dogs — I cannot satisfy endless demands!"

sentences.zh: 待使者甚薄；

translations.literal: He treated the envoy very poorly;
translations.idiomatic: He treated the envoy contemptuously;

sentences.zh: 使者還，語諧之曰：「柏年云：『胡諧之何物狗！

translations.literal: the envoy returned and told Xiezhi: "Bonian said: 'What sort of cur is Hu Xiezhi!
translations.idiomatic: the envoy reported to Xiezhi that Bonian had called him "some sort of cur

sentences.zh: 所求無厭！』

translations.literal: His demands know no end!'
translations.idiomatic: whose "demands know no end."

sentences.zh: 」諧之恨之，譖於上曰：「柏年恃險聚眾，欲專據一州。」

translations.literal: Xiezhi bore a grudge and slandered him to the emperor, saying: "Bonian relies on perilous terrain, gathers troops, and wishes to hold a whole province for himself."
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhi bore a grudge and slandered Bonian to the emperor, saying he was gathering troops in the mountains to seize the province for himself."

sentences.zh: 上使雍州刺史南郡王長懋誘柏年，啟爲府長史。

translations.literal: The emperor had Prince Changmao of Nankang, Governor of Yongzhou, lure Bonian and report him as Chief of Staff of the princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Prince Changmao of Nankang lure Bonian to his staff as chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 柏年至襄陽，上欲不問，諧之曰：「見虎格得，而縱上山乎？」

translations.literal: When Bonian reached Xiangyang, the emperor wished to let the matter pass; Xiezhi said: "When you have seized a tiger, do you let it back up the mountain?"
translations.idiomatic: When Bonian reached Xiangyang, the emperor wished to spare him; Xiezhi said, "When you have caught a tiger, do you let it back up the mountain?"

sentences.zh: 甲午，賜柏年死。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Bonian was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Bonian was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 李烏奴叛入氐，依楊文弘，引氐兵千餘人寇梁州，陷白馬戍。

translations.literal: Li Wunu rebelled and entered the Di, relying on Yang Wenhong; he led more than a thousand Di troops to raid Liangzhou and took Baima Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wunu rebelled, joined the Di under Yang Wenhong, and with more than a thousand Di warriors raided Liangzhou and captured Baima Garrison.

sentences.zh: 王玄邈使人詐降誘烏奴，烏奴輕兵襲州城，玄邈伏兵邀擊，大破之，烏奴挺身復走入氐。

translations.literal: Wang Xuanmiao sent men to feign surrender and lure Wunu; Wunu led light troops in a surprise attack on the provincial capital; Xuanmiao's ambush intercepted and routed them; Wunu alone escaped and fled back among the Di.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanmiao feigned surrender to lure Wunu into a light attack on the capital; his ambush routed the raiders, and Wunu alone fled back to the Di.

sentences.zh: 初，玄邈爲青州刺史，上在淮陰，爲宋太宗所疑，欲北附魏，遣書結玄邈，玄邈長史清河房叔安曰：「將軍居方州之重，無故舉忠孝而棄之，三齊之土，寧蹈東海而死耳，不敢隨將軍也！」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xuanmiao was Inspector of Qingzhou, the emperor was at Huaiyin, suspected by Emperor Ming of Song, and wished to go north and attach himself to Wei; he sent a letter to win over Xuanmiao. Xuanmiao's Chief of Staff Fang Shuan of Qinghe said: "General, you hold the weight of a provincial command — to abandon loyalty and filial piety without cause: the people of the Three Qis would rather throw themselves into the Eastern Sea and die than follow you!"
translations.idiomatic: Years before, when Xuanmiao was inspector of Qingzhou, the future emperor at Huaiyin, suspect in the eyes of Emperor Ming, had written inviting him to defect to Wei. Xuanmiao's chief of staff Fang Shuan protested: "You hold a great provincial command — the people of the Three Qis would drown themselves in the Eastern Sea rather than follow you in abandoning loyalty!"

sentences.zh: 玄邈乃不答上書。

translations.literal: Xuanmiao then did not reply to the emperor's letter.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmiao ignored the letter.

sentences.zh: 及罷州還，至淮陰，嚴軍直過；

translations.literal: When he left his province and returned, passing Huaiyin, he marched his army straight through in strict array;
translations.idiomatic: When he later passed through Huaiyin on his way home, he marched past in full battle order;

sentences.zh: 至建康，啟太宗，稱上有異志。

translations.literal: reaching Jiankang, he reported to Emperor Ming that the emperor harbored disloyal intent.
translations.idiomatic: and at Jiankang reported to Emperor Ming that the man had treasonous designs.

sentences.zh: 及上爲驃騎，引爲司馬，玄邈甚懼，而上待之如初。

translations.literal: When the emperor became General of Agile Cavalry, he summoned Xuanmiao as Marshal; Xuanmiao was greatly afraid, but the emperor treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor became General of Agile Cavalry, he summoned Xuanmiao as his marshal; Xuanmiao was terrified, but the emperor treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 及破烏奴，上曰：「玄邈果不負吾意遇也。」

translations.literal: When Wunu was defeated, the emperor said: "Xuanmiao has indeed not betrayed how I wished to treat him."
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Wunu, the emperor said, "Xuanmiao has indeed proved worthy of how I treated him."

sentences.zh: 叔安爲寧蜀太守，上賞其忠正，欲用爲梁州，會病卒。

translations.literal: Shuan was Administrator of Ningshu; the emperor rewarded his loyalty and rectitude and wished to use him in Liangzhou, but he died of illness in the meantime.
translations.idiomatic: Shuan became administrator of Ningshu; the emperor wished to reward his loyalty with Liangzhou, but he died of illness before the appointment.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛亥，立皇太子妃斐氏。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on xinhai, the crown prince's consort, the Lady Pei, was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on xinhai, the crown prince's consort, Lady Pei, was formally invested.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，魏遣假梁郡王嘉督二將出淮陰，隴西公琛督三將出廣陵，河東公薛虎子督三將出壽陽，奉丹楊王劉昶入寇；

translations.literal: On guichou, Wei sent Acting Prince Jia of Liang Commandery with two generals out from Huaiyin, Duke Chen of Longxi with three generals out from Guangling, and Duke Xue Huzi of Hedong with three generals out from Shouyang, escorting Prince Liu Chang of Danyang in invasion;
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Wei sent Prince Jia of Liang with two generals from Huaiyin, Duke Chen of Longxi with three from Guangling, and Duke Xue Huzi of Hedong with three from Shouyang, escorting Liu Chang of Danyang in an invasion;

sentences.zh: 許昶以克復舊業，世胙江南，稱籓於魏。

translations.literal: Chang was promised recovery of his former enterprise and hereditary sacrifice in the lands south of the Yangtze, and he declared himself a vassal of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was promised restoration to the throne south of the Yangtze and acknowledged Wei as his suzerain.

sentences.zh: 蠻酋桓誕請爲前驅，以誕爲南征西道大都督。

translations.literal: The barbarian chieftain Huan Dan asked to serve as vanguard; Dan was made Grand Commander of the Southern Expedition Western Route.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal chieftain Huan Dan volunteered as vanguard and was made grand commander of the western wing of the southern expedition.

sentences.zh: 義陽民謝天蓋自稱司州刺史，欲以州附魏，魏樂陵鎮將韋珍引兵渡淮應接。

translations.literal: Xie Tiangai of Yiyang styled himself Inspector of Sizhou and wished to attach his province to Wei; Wei Garrison General Wei Zhen of Leling led troops across the Huai to link up with him.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Tiangai of Yiyang declared himself inspector of Sizhou and offered to defect to Wei; Wei Zhen of Leling crossed the Huai to support him.

sentences.zh: 豫章王嶷遣中兵參軍蕭惠朗將二千人，助司州刺史蕭景先討天蓋，韋珍略七千餘戶而去。

translations.literal: Prince Yan of Yuzhang sent Central Army Major Xiao Huilang with two thousand men to aid Inspector Xiao Jingxian of Sizhou in attacking Tiangai; Wei Zhen plundered more than seven thousand households and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yan sent Xiao Huilang with two thousand men to aid Inspector Xiao Jingxian against Tiangai; Wei Zhen carried off more than seven thousand households and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 景先，上之從子也。

translations.literal: Jingxian was a nephew of the emperor on his father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian was the emperor's nephew.

sentences.zh: 南兗州刺史王敬則聞魏將濟淮，委鎮還建康，士民驚散，既而魏竟不至。

translations.literal: Wang Jingze, Inspector of South Yanzhou, hearing that Wei would cross the Huai, abandoned his post and returned to Jiankang; gentry and people fled in alarm — yet in the end Wei did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingze, inspector of South Yanzhou, hearing that Wei would cross the Huai, abandoned his post and fled to Jiankang, throwing the region into panic — yet in the end the northerners never came.

sentences.zh: 上以其功臣，不問。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering him a meritorious official, did not question him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor let the matter pass, treating Wang Jingze as a servant who had earned his grace.

sentences.zh: 上之輔宋也，遣驍騎將軍王洪範使柔然，約與共攻魏。

translations.literal: When the emperor was assisting Song, he sent Swift Cavalry General Wang Hongfan as envoy to the Rouran, agreeing to join in a joint attack on Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When the future emperor was still serving Song, he had sent Wang Hongfan as envoy to Rouran to arrange a joint campaign against Wei.

sentences.zh: 洪範自蜀出吐谷渾，歷西域，乃得達。

translations.literal: Hongfan went out from Shu through Tuyuhun, passed through the Western Regions, and only then arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Hongfan had left through Shu, crossed Tuyuhun and the Western Regions, and only then reached them.

sentences.zh: 至是，柔然十餘萬騎寇魏，至塞上而還。

translations.literal: At this time, more than a hundred thousand Rouran horsemen raided Wei, reaching the frontier defenses and returning.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Rouran had sent more than a hundred thousand horsemen against Wei, who reached the border and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏詔中書監高允議定律令。

translations.literal: That year, Wei decreed that Secretariat Director Gao Yun should deliberate on establishing laws and statutes.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wei ordered Gao Yun, director of the Secretariat, to draft revised laws.

sentences.zh: 允雖篤老，而志識不衰。

translations.literal: Although Yun was deeply aged, his will and understanding did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: Though Gao Yun was very old, his mind remained sharp.

sentences.zh: 詔以允家貧養薄，令樂部絲竹十人五日一詣允以娛其志，朝晡給膳，朔望致牛酒，月給衣服綿絹；

translations.literal: An imperial decree held that Yun's family was poor and his stipend thin; he was ordered ten musicians from the Music Office to visit him every five days to delight his spirit; morning and evening meals were supplied, beef and wine on the new and full moon, and clothing, silk, and cotton monthly;
translations.idiomatic: The court, finding his household poor and his stipend meager, sent ten musicians from the Music Office every five days for his pleasure, supplied two meals daily, beef and wine on the first and fifteenth, and monthly rations of cloth and silk;

sentences.zh: 入見則備幾杖，問以政治。

translations.literal: When he came for audience, a couch and staff were prepared, and he was questioned about governance.
translations.idiomatic: At imperial audiences he was given a seat and staff and consulted on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 契丹莫賀弗勿干帥部落萬餘口入附於魏，居白狼水東。

translations.literal: The Khitan mohuo-fu Wugan led more than ten thousand people of his tribe to submit to Wei and settle east of the White Wolf River.
translations.idiomatic: Wugan, mohuo-fu of the Khitan, led more than ten thousand tribesmen to submit to Wei and settle east of the White Wolf River.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊戌朔，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the wuxu day, new moon, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon of the first month in spring, a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 以司空褚淵爲司徒，尚書右僕射王儉爲左僕射；

translations.literal: Minister of Works Chu Yuan was made Minister of Education; Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Jian was made Left Vice Director;
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan was promoted from minister of works to minister of education, and Wang Jian from right to left vice director of the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 淵不受。

translations.literal: Yuan did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，上祀南郊。

translations.literal: On xinchou, the emperor performed the southern border sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 魏隴西公琛等攻拔馬頭戍，殺太守劉從。

translations.literal: Duke Chen of Longxi and others in Wei attacked and took Matou Garrison, killing Administrator Liu Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Duke Chen of Longxi and others captured Matou Garrison and killed its administrator Liu Cong.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，詔內外纂嚴，發兵拒魏，征南郡王長懋爲中軍將軍，鎮石頭。

translations.literal: On yimao, an edict ordered strict guard throughout court and countryside, troops raised to resist Wei, and Prince Changmao of Nankang summoned as General of the Central Army to garrison Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the court mobilized for war, summoned troops against Wei, and posted Prince Changmao of Nankang at Shitou as general of the central army.

sentences.zh: 魏廣川王略卒。

translations.literal: Prince Lüe of Guangchuan in Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Prince Lüe of Guangchuan died.

sentences.zh: 魏師攻鐘離，徐州刺史崔文仲擊破之。

translations.literal: Wei troops attacked Zhongli; Cui Wenzhong, Inspector of Xuzhou, defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei attacked Zhongli, Xuzhou inspector Cui Wenzhong routed them.

sentences.zh: 文仲遣軍主崔孝伯渡淮，攻魏茌眉戍主龍得侯等，殺之。

translations.literal: Wenzhong sent Commander Cui Xiaobo to cross the Huai and attack the Wei garrison chiefs Long Dehou and others at Chimei, killing them.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong sent Cui Xiaobo across the Huai to attack the Chimei garrison and kill its commander Long Dehou and his men.

sentences.zh: 文仲，祖思之族人也。

translations.literal: Wenzhong was a clansman of Zusi.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Wenzhong was a kinsman of the Cui clan of Qinghe, to which Zusi belonged.

sentences.zh: 群蠻依阻山谷，連帶荊、湘、雍、郢、司五州之境，聞魏師入寇，官盡發民丁，南襄城蠻秦遠乘虛寇潼陽，殺縣令。

translations.literal: Barbarian tribes relying on mountain valleys spanned the borders of Jing, Xiang, Yong, Ying, and Si; hearing that Wei troops were invading, the government conscripted every available man; Qin Yuan of the Nanxiangcheng barbarians seized the moment to raid Tongyang, killing the magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal peoples held the mountain valleys across five provinces; when Wei invaded, the state drafted every able man; Qin Yuan of the Nanxiang barbarians seized the chance to raid Tongyang and kill its magistrate.

sentences.zh: 司州蠻引魏兵寇平昌，平昌戍主苟元賓擊破之。

translations.literal: The Si province barbarians led Wei troops to raid Pingchang; Garrison Chief Gou Yuanbin defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Si province tribes guided Wei raiders against Pingchang, but garrison chief Gou Yuanbin beat them off.

sentences.zh: 北上黃蠻文勉德寇汶陽，汶陽太守戴元賓棄城奔江陵，豫章王嶷遣中兵參軍劉伾緒將千人討之，至當陽，勉德請降，秦遠遁去。

translations.literal: Wen Miande of the Beishanghuang barbarians raided Wenyang; Administrator Dai Yuanbin abandoned the city and fled to Jiangling; Prince Yan of Yuzhang sent Central Army Major Liu Pixu with a thousand men to suppress them; reaching Dangyang, Miande sought surrender and Qin Yuan fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Miande of the Beishanghuang tribes raided Wenyang; Administrator Dai Yuanbin fled to Jiangling; Prince Yan sent Liu Pixu with a thousand men; at Dangyang Miande submitted and Qin Yuan escaped.

sentences.zh: 魏將薛道標引兵趣壽陽，上使齊郡太守劉懷慰作冠軍將軍薛淵書以招道標；

translations.literal: Wei General Xue Daobiao led troops toward Shouyang; the emperor had Liu Huaiwei, Administrator of Qi Commandery, forge a letter from Champion General Xue Yuan to recruit Daobiao;
translations.idiomatic: As Xue Daobiao of Wei marched on Shouyang, the emperor had Liu Huaiwei forge a letter in the name of Xue Yuan to entice him to defect;

sentences.zh: 魏人聞之，召道標還，使梁郡王嘉代之。

translations.literal: When the northerners heard of it, they recalled Daobiao and replaced him with Prince Jia of Liang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wei heard of the ruse, recalled Daobiao, and sent Prince Jia of Liang in his place.

sentences.zh: 懷慰，乘民之子也。

translations.literal: Huaiwei was a son of Chen Min.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huaiwei was the son of Chen Min.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁卯朔，嘉與劉昶寇壽陽。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the dingmao day, new moon, Jia and Liu Chang raided Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the new moon of the second month, Jia and Liu Chang attacked Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 將戰，昶四向拜將士，流涕縱橫，曰：「願同戮力，以雪仇恥！」

translations.literal: About to give battle, Chang bowed in the four directions to his officers and soldiers, tears streaming, saying: "I wish that together we may exert our strength to wash away shame and hatred!
translations.idiomatic: Before battle Liu Chang bowed to his troops on every side, weeping, and said, "Let us fight as one to avenge our disgrace!

translations.literal: Closing quotation.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation.

sentences.zh: 魏步騎號二十萬，豫州刺史垣崇祖集文武議之，欲治外城，堰肥水以自固。

translations.literal: Wei's infantry and cavalry, said to number two hundred thousand, arrived; Yuan Chongzu, Inspector of Yuzhou, assembled civil and military officers to deliberate; he wished to repair the outer wall and dam the Fei River to strengthen his defense.
translations.idiomatic: With two hundred thousand Wei foot and horse at hand, Yuzhou inspector Yuan Chongzu consulted his staff on damming the Fei River and holding the outer walls.

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「昔佛狸入寇，南平王士卒完盛，數倍於今，猶以郭大難守，退保內城。

translations.literal: All said: "Formerly when Bulai invaded, Prince Nanping's garrison was complete and strong, several times what it is now, yet because the outer city was too large to defend, they withdrew to the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: All said, "When Bulai invaded, Nanping had several times our present force yet still abandoned the outer city for the inner citadel.

sentences.zh: 且自有肥水，未嘗堰也，恐勞而無益。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the Fei River has always been there — it has never been dammed; I fear the labor would be to no avail.
translations.idiomatic: And the Fei has never been dammed — the work may be wasted.

sentences.zh: 崇祖曰：「若棄外城，虜必據之，外修樓櫓，內築長圍，則坐成擒矣。

translations.literal: Chongzu said: "If we abandon the outer city, the enemy will occupy it; repairing towers and building a long encirclement inside, we will simply be captured sitting down.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzu replied, "Yield the outer city and they will fortify it and ring the inner walls — we would be caught without a fight.

sentences.zh: 守郭築堰，是吾不諫之策也。」

translations.literal: Holding the outer wall and building the dam — this is the tactic I will not advise against.
translations.idiomatic: Defend the walls and dam the river — that is the plan I mean to follow.

sentences.zh: 乃於城西北堰肥水，堰北築小城，周爲深塹，使數千人守之，曰：「虜見城小，以爲一舉可取，必悉力攻之，以謀破堰；

translations.literal: Thereupon at the northwest of the city he dammed the Fei River; north of the dam he built a small city encircled by a deep moat, with several thousand men to guard it, saying: "When the enemy sees the small city and thinks it can be taken in one stroke, they will surely exert their full strength to attack it, intending to break the dam;
translations.idiomatic: He dammed the Fei northwest of the city, built a small fort north of the dam with a deep trench, manned it with thousands, and said, "They will see a small target, think it easy prey, and throw everything at it to break the dam —

sentences.zh: 吾縱水沖之，皆爲流屍矣。」

translations.literal: I will release the water to rush against them — all will become floating corpses.
translations.idiomatic: then I will flood them and leave nothing but corpses in the ditch.

sentences.zh: 魏人果蟻附攻小城，崇祖著白紗帽，肩輿上城，晡時，決堰下水；

translations.literal: The northerners indeed swarmed like ants to attack the small city; Chongzu wore a white gauze cap and rode in a shoulder-litter up onto the wall; at the end of the afternoon watch he broke the dam and released the water downstream;
translations.idiomatic: The northerners did swarm the small fort; Chongzu, in a white gauze cap, was carried aloft on the walls; in late afternoon he broke the dam.

sentences.zh: 魏攻城之眾漂墜塹中，人馬溺死以千數。

translations.literal: The Wei troops attacking the city were swept into the moat and drowned; men and horses died by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of men and horses were swept into the moat and drowned.

sentences.zh: 魏師退走。

translations.literal: The Wei army withdrew and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army retreated.

sentences.zh: 謝天蓋部曲殺天蓋以降。

translations.literal: Xie Tiangai's personal followers killed Tiangai and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Tiangai's own troops killed him and defected.

sentences.zh: 宋自孝建以來，政綱弛紊，簿籍訛謬，上詔黃門郎會稽虞玩之等更加檢定，曰：「黃籍，民之大紀，國之治端。

translations.literal: Since Xiaojian in Song, the political framework had slackened and become disordered, registers and records were erroneous; the emperor decreed that Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yu Wanzi of Kuaiji and others should conduct further verification, saying: "The yellow registers are the great charter of the people and the beginning of good governance for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Xiaojian's day Song's registers had decayed; the emperor ordered Yu Wanzi and others to audit them, declaring, "The yellow registers are the people's charter and the foundation of rule.

sentences.zh: 自頃巧偽日甚，何以釐革？」

translations.literal: Recently crafty falsification grows daily — how can it be rectified?
translations.idiomatic: Fraud grows worse daily — how shall we reform it?

sentences.zh: 玩之上表，以爲：「元嘉中，故光祿大夫傅隆年出七十，猶手自書籍，躬加隱校。

translations.literal: Wanzi submitted a memorial, holding: "In the yuannian reign, the former Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Fu Long, though over seventy, still personally wrote registers and personally carried out concealed verification.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wanzi replied that in Yuannian even Fu Long at seventy had still copied and checked the rolls by hand.

sentences.zh: 今欲求治取正，必在勤明令長。

translations.literal: Now if we wish to seek good order and take what is correct, the essential lies in diligent and clear district magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: True reform depends on diligent, conscientious magistrates.

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜以元嘉二十七年籍爲正，更立明科，一聽首悔；

translations.literal: In my humble view, the register of the twenty-seventh year of Yuannian should be taken as standard; a clear statute should be newly established, and all should be allowed to confess first;
translations.idiomatic: I propose taking the Yuannian 27 register as the standard, offering amnesty to those who confess,

sentences.zh: 迷而不返，依制必戮；

translations.literal: those deluded who do not return, according to regulation will surely be executed;
translations.idiomatic: and executing those who persist in fraud;

sentences.zh: 若有虛昧，州縣同科。」

translations.literal: if there is concealment or obfuscation, province and district share the same penalty.
translations.idiomatic: holding provinces and districts equally liable for concealed fraud.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 上以群蠻數爲叛亂，分荊、益置巴州以鎮之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the barbarian tribes repeatedly rebelled, divided Jing and Yi to establish Bazhou to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: To suppress recurring tribal revolts, the emperor carved Bazhou out of Jing and Yi.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以三巴校尉明慧昭爲巴州刺史，領巴東太守。

translations.literal: On renshen, Three-Ba Commandant Ming Huizhao was made Inspector of Bazhou, concurrently Administrator of Badong.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Ming Huizhao became inspector of Bazhou and administrator of Badong.

sentences.zh: 是時，齊之境內，有州二十三，郡三百九十，縣千四百八十五。

translations.literal: At this time, within the borders of Qi, there were twenty-three provinces, three hundred ninety commanderies, and one thousand four hundred eighty-five counties.
translations.idiomatic: Qi at this time comprised twenty-three provinces, 390 commanderies, and 1,485 counties.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，崔文仲遣軍主陳靖拔魏竹邑，殺戍主白仲都；

translations.literal: On yiyou, Cui Wenzhong sent Commander Chen Jing to take Wei's Zhuyi, killing Garrison Chief Bai Zhongdu;
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou Cui Wenzhong's Chen Jing captured Wei's Zhuyi and killed its garrison chief Bai Zhongdu;

sentences.zh: 崔叔延破魏睢陵，殺淮陽太守梁惡。

translations.literal: Cui Shuyan took Wei's Suiling, killing Administrator of Huaiyang Liang E.
translations.idiomatic: while Cui Shuyan took Suiling and killed Huaiyang administrator Liang E.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁酉朔，以侍中西昌侯鸞爲郢州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the dingyou day, new moon, Attendant-in-Ordinary Luan, Marquis of Xichang, was made Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the third month's new moon, Luan, marquis of Xichang and attendant-in-ordinary, became inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 鸞，帝兄始安貞王道生之子也，早孤，爲帝所養，恩過諸子。

translations.literal: Luan was the son of Prince Daosheng of Shian, the emperor's elder brother; orphaned early, he was reared by the emperor, whose favor for him exceeded that for his own sons.
translations.idiomatic: Luan was the orphaned son of the emperor's elder brother Prince Daosheng; the emperor had raised him with more affection than his own sons.

sentences.zh: 魏劉昶以雨水方降，表請還師，魏人許之；

translations.literal: Liu Chang of Wei, because heavy rains were falling, memorialized requesting withdrawal of the army; the northerners permitted it;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang, citing the rains, asked Wei to let him withdraw; permission was granted;

sentences.zh: 丙午，遣車騎大將軍馮熙將兵迎之。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry Feng Xi was sent to lead troops to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: and on bingwu Feng Xi marched out to escort him home.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛巳，魏主如白登山；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinsi, the Wei emperor went to White Horse Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer the Wei emperor visited White Horse Mountain;

sentences.zh: 五月，丙申朔，如火山；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the bingchen day, new moon, he went to Fire Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: at the fifth month's new moon he went to Fire Mountain;

sentences.zh: 壬寅，還平城。

translations.literal: On renyin, he returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: and on renyin returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 自晉以來，建康宮之外城唯設竹籬，而有六門。

translations.literal: Since the Jin dynasty, outside the Jiankang palace only bamboo palisades had been set, with six gates in all.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jin times Jiankang's outer palace had been fenced with bamboo, with only six gates.

sentences.zh: 會有發白虎樽者，言「白門三重關，竹籬穿不完」。
