translations.literal: It happened that someone opened a white tiger offering-jar and spoke: "White Gate's threefold passes — bamboo palisades cannot stand complete."
translations.idiomatic: Someone opening a white-tiger offering-vessel found a prophecy: "Three gates at White Gate — bamboo fences will not hold."

sentences.zh: 上感其言，命改立都牆。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved by the words and ordered the capital wall rebuilt in stone.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by the omen, the emperor ordered a proper city wall built.

sentences.zh: 李烏奴數乘間出寇梁州，豫章王嶷遣中兵參軍王圖南，將益州兵從劍閣掩擊之；

translations.literal: Li Wunu repeatedly seized opportunities to raid Liangzhou; Prince Yan of Yuzhang sent Central Army Major Wang Tunan with Yi province troops to strike from Jian'ge by a concealed route;
translations.idiomatic: Li Wunu kept raiding Liangzhou; Prince Yan sent Wang Tunan through Jian'ge with Yi troops in a flank attack;

sentences.zh: 梁、南秦二州刺史崔慧景發梁州兵屯白馬，與圖南覆背擊烏奴，大破之，烏奴走保武興。

translations.literal: Cui Huijing, Inspector of Liang and South Qin, mobilized Liangzhou troops to encamp at Baima and, with Tunan, struck Wunu from front and rear, greatly defeating him; Wunu fled to hold Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Huijing camped at Baima and, with Tunan attacking front and rear, routed Wunu, who fled to Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 慧景，祖思之族人也。

translations.literal: Huijing was a clansman of Zusi.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Huijing was another kinsman of Zusi's clan.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛亥，魏主如火山。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinhai, the Wei emperor went to Fire Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Wei emperor again visited Fire Mountain.

sentences.zh: 戊午，皇太子穆妃裴氏卒。

translations.literal: On wuwu, the crown prince's consort, the Lady Pei, died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Lady Pei, consort of the crown prince, died.

sentences.zh: 詔南郡王長懋移鎮西州。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Prince Changmao of Nankang to move his garrison to West Province.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Changmao of Nankang was ordered to shift his command to West Province.

sentences.zh: 角城戍主舉城降魏；

translations.literal: The garrison chief of Jiaocheng surrendered the city to Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Jiaocheng's garrison chief surrendered to Wei;

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，丁酉，魏遣徐州刺史梁郡王嘉迎之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on dingyou, Wei sent Administrator of Xuzhou Prince Jia of Liang Commandery to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: and in the eighth month Prince Jia of Liang, Wei's inspector of Xuzhou, came to take possession.

sentences.zh: 又遣平南將軍郎大檀等三將出朐城，將軍白吐頭等二將出海西，將軍元泰等二將出連口，將軍封延等三將出角城，鎮南將軍賀羅出下蔡，同入寇。

translations.literal: They also sent General of Pacifying the South Lang Datan with three generals out from Jucheng, General Bai Tutou with two generals out from Haixi, General Yuan Tai with two generals out from Lian Pass, General Feng Yan with three generals out from Jiaocheng, and General of Pacifying the South Heluo out from Xia'ai — all entering to raid together.
translations.idiomatic: Wei also sent five columns — Lang Datan from Jucheng, Bai Tutou from Haixi, Yuan Tai from Lian Pass, Feng Yan from Jiaocheng, Heluo from Xia'ai — in a coordinated invasion.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，魏主如方山；

translations.literal: On jiachen, the Wei emperor went to Square Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the Wei emperor went to Square Mountain;

sentences.zh: 戊申，游武州山石窟寺。

translations.literal: On wushen, he toured the cliff-temple at Wuzhou Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: on wushen toured the cave temples at Wuzhou Mountain;

sentences.zh: 庚戌，還平城。

translations.literal: On gengxu, he returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: and on gengxu returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景遣長史裴叔保攻李烏奴於武興，爲氐王楊文弘所敗。

translations.literal: Cui Huijing sent Chief of Staff Pei Shubao to attack Li Wunu at Wuxing and was defeated by the Di king Yang Wenhong.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Huijing's Pei Shubao besieged Wunu at Wuxing but was beaten by the Di king Yang Wenhong.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲午朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the jiawu day, new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: At the ninth month's new moon there was an eclipse of the sun.

sentences.zh: 丙午，柔然遣使來聘。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Rouran sent envoys on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Rouran sent envoys.

sentences.zh: 汝南太守常元真、龍驤將軍胡青苟降於魏。

translations.literal: Administrator of Runan Chang Yuanzhen and General of the Flying Dragons Hu Qinggou defected to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Runan administrator Chang Yuanzhen and General Hu Qinggou defected to Wei.

sentences.zh: 閏月，辛巳，遣領軍李安民循行清、泗諸戍以備魏。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on xinsi, General of the Palace Guard Li Anmin was sent to inspect the garrisons along the Qing and Si to guard against Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the leap month Li Anmin was dispatched to inspect Qing and Si garrisons against Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏梁郡王嘉帥眾十萬圍朐山，朐山戍主玄元度嬰城固守，青、冀二州刺史范陽盧紹之遣子奐將兵助之。

translations.literal: Prince Jia of Liang Commandery in Wei led a hundred thousand troops to besiege Qushan; Garrison Chief Xuan Yuandu defended the city stubbornly; Lu Shaozhi of Fanyang, Inspector of Qing and Ji, sent his son Huan with troops to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jia besieged Qushan with a hundred thousand men; Xuan Yuandu held the city; inspectors Lu Shaozhi's son Huan marched to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，元度大破魏師。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Yuandu greatly defeated the Wei army.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Yuandu routed the Wei besiegers.

sentences.zh: 台遣軍主崔靈建等將萬餘人自淮入海，夜至，各舉兩炬；

translations.literal: The capital sent Commander Cui Lingjian and others with more than ten thousand men from the Huai by sea; arriving at night, each raised two torches;
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Cui Lingjian with ten thousand men by sea from the Huai; they arrived by night, each man carrying two torches;

sentences.zh: 魏師望見，遁去。

translations.literal: When the Wei army saw them, they fled away.
translations.idiomatic: and at the sight the Wei army fled.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，王儉固請解選職，許之；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Wang Jian urgently and repeatedly requested release from his selection duties; it was granted;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Wang Jian repeatedly asked to be relieved of personnel selection; the emperor agreed;

sentences.zh: 加儉侍中，以太子詹事何戢領選。

translations.literal: Jian was additionally made Attendant-in-Ordinary, and He Yan, Supervisor of the Crown Prince's Household, took over selection.
translations.idiomatic: made him attendant-in-ordinary, and put He Yan in charge of appointments.

sentences.zh: 上以戢資重，欲加常待，褚淵曰：「聖旨每以蟬冕不宜過多。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Yan's qualifications were weighty, wished to add Attendant-in-Ordinary; Chu Yuan said: "Your Majesty's intent each time is that cicada-crown offices should not be too many.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to give He Yan the attendant title as well; Chu Yuan objected, "Your Majesty has always held that there should not be too many cicada-crowned courtiers.

sentences.zh: 臣與王儉既已左珥，若復加戢，則八座遂有三貂；

translations.literal: Your servant and Wang Jian have already worn them on the left ear; if Yan is also added, then of the eight seats there would be three sable-tailed officials;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian and I already wear one; a third on the eight chief ministers would be excessive;

sentences.zh: 若帖以驍、游，亦爲不少。」

translations.literal: If one added swift-cavalry and roaming-palace posts, that too would not be few.
translations.idiomatic: and swift-cavalry and palace posts would still leave the senior ranks crowded.

sentences.zh: 乃以戢爲吏部尚書，加驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yan was made Director of the Board of Civil Office and additionally Swift Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan was made director of the Board of Civil Office and general of swift cavalry instead.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以沙州刺史楊廣香爲西秦州刺史，又以其子炅爲武都太守。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Administrator of Shazhou Yang Guangxiang was made Inspector of West Qinzhou, and his son Jiong was also made Administrator of Wudou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Yang Guangxiang became inspector of West Qinzhou and his son Jiong administrator of Wudou.

sentences.zh: 丁未，魏以昌黎王馮熙爲西道都督，與征南將軍桓誕出義陽，鎮南將軍賀羅出鐘離，同入寇。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Wei made Prince Xi of Changli Western Route Commander-in-Chief and, with General of the Southern Expedition Huan Dan, went out from Yiyang; General of Pacifying the South Heluo went out from Zhongli — all entering to raid together.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Wei launched another invasion: Feng Xi commanded the western route with Huan Dan from Yiyang, Heluo from Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 淮北四州民不樂屬魏，常思歸江南，上多遣間諜誘之。

translations.literal: The people of the four provinces north of the Huai did not rejoice in belonging to Wei and constantly longed to return to the lands south of the Yangtze; the emperor frequently sent spies to entice them.
translations.idiomatic: North Huai peoples chafed under Wei and longed for the south; the emperor sent agents to stir them up.

sentences.zh: 於是，徐州民桓標之、兗州民徐猛子等所在蜂起爲寇盜，聚眾保伍固，推司馬朗之爲主。

translations.literal: Thereupon Huan Biaozhi of Xuzhou, Xu Mengzi of Yanzhou, and others everywhere rose like bees as bandits, gathering troops and holding Wu Fort, making Sima Langzhi their leader.
translations.idiomatic: Then Xuzhou's Huan Biaozhi, Yanzhou's Xu Mengzi, and others rose across the region, seized Wu Fort, and made Sima Langzhi their chief.

sentences.zh: 魏遣淮陽王尉元、平南將軍薛虎子等討之。

translations.literal: Wei sent Prince Yuanyuan of Huaiyang, General of Pacifying the South Xue Huzi, and others to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent Prince Yuanyuan of Huaiyang and Xue Huzi to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊寅，丹陽尹王僧虔上言：「郡縣獄相承有上湯殺囚，名爲救疾，實行冤暴。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on wuyin, Administrator of Danyang Wang Sengqian submitted a statement: "Commandery and district prisons successively follow the practice of superior boiling to kill prisoners, called 'saving urgency,' but in reality carry out wrongful violence.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Danyang prefect Wang Sengqian protested that local jails routinely boiled sick prisoners alive, calling it "urgent relief" but practicing gross injustice.

sentences.zh: 豈有死生大命，而潛制下邑！

translations.literal: How can the great mandate of life and death be secretly controlled by lower districts!
translations.idiomatic: Life and death are the state's prerogative — no county may usurp them in secret!

sentences.zh: 愚謂囚病必先刺郡，求職司與醫對共診驗，遠縣家人省視，然後處治。」

translations.literal: In my humble view, when a prisoner is ill, the district must first report to the commandery; a responsible official together with a physician should jointly examine and verify; distant counties should allow family viewing — only then should punishment be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Sick prisoners should be reported to the commandery, jointly diagnosed, and seen by kin before any sentence is carried out.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以楊難當之孫後起爲北秦州刺史、武都王，鎮武興。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Yang Nandang's grandson Houqi was made Inspector of North Qinzhou and Prince of Wudou, garrisoning Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Houqi, grandson of Yang Nandang, became prince of Wudou and inspector of North Qinzhou at Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊戌，以司空褚淵爲司徒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on wuxu, Minister of Works Chu Yuan was made Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Chu Yuan at last accepted appointment as minister of education.

sentences.zh: 淵入朝，以腰扇障日，征虜功曹劉祥從側過，曰：「作如上舉止，羞面見人，扇障何益！」

translations.literal: Yuan entered court, using a waist fan to shield his face from the sun. Liu Xiang, registrar of the Conquering Barbarians staff, passed by at his side and said: "With deportment like that, what shame to show your face in public—what use is a fan as a screen!
translations.idiomatic: When Chu Yuan came to court shading his face with a waist fan, Liu Xiang of the Conquering Barbarians staff passed beside him and said, "Act like that and you ought to be ashamed to show your face—what good is hiding behind a fan?"

sentences.zh: 淵曰：「寒士不遜！」

translations.literal: Yuan said: "Ill-bred petty clerk!"
translations.idiomatic: You impudent clerk!" Yuan snapped."

sentences.zh: 祥曰：「不能殺袁、劉，安得免寒士！」

translations.literal: Xiang said: "If you could not kill Yuan and Liu, how can you escape being a petty clerk!"
translations.idiomatic: If you could not kill Yuan and Liu, how are you anything but a petty clerk!" Xiang retorted.

sentences.zh: 祥，穆之之孫也。

translations.literal: Xiang was the grandson of Muzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was a grandson of Liu Muzhi.

sentences.zh: 祥好文學，而性韻剛疏，撰《宋書》，譏斥禪代；

translations.literal: Xiang loved literature, but his temperament was blunt and unrestrained; he wrote the History of Song, mocking the transfer of the mandate;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was a literary man, blunt and unrestrained by nature; in his History of Song he mocked the abdication that had brought Qi to power;

sentences.zh: 王儉密以聞，坐徙廣州而卒。

translations.literal: Wang Jian secretly reported this; he was punished by exile to Guangzhou and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian reported him in secret, and he was exiled to Guangzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 太子宴朝臣於玄圃，右衛率沈文季與褚淵語相失，文季怒曰：「淵自謂忠臣，不知死之日何面目見宋明帝！」

translations.literal: The crown prince entertained the court at the Mystic Orchard. Right Guard Commander Shen Wenji exchanged harsh words with Chu Yuan; enraged, Wenji said: "Yuan calls himself a loyal minister—on the day he dies, what face will he show to Emperor Ming of Song!
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet for the court in the Mystic Orchard, Right Guard Commander Shen Wenji quarreled bitterly with Chu Yuan and cried out, "Yuan calls himself loyal—when he dies, what face will he show Emperor Ming of Song?"

sentences.zh: 太子笑曰：「沈率醉矣」

translations.literal: The crown prince laughed and said: "Commander Shen is drunk."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince laughed and said, "Commander Shen is drunk."

sentences.zh: 壬子，以豫章王嶷爲中書監、司空、揚州刺史，以臨川王映爲都督荊、雍等九州諸軍事、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: On renzi, Prince of Yuzhang Liao was made Director of the Secretariat, Minister of Works, and Inspector of Yangzhou; Prince of Linchuan Ying was made Commander over nine provinces including Jing and Yong, and Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Prince Liao of Yuzhang was made director of the Secretariat, minister of works, and inspector of Yangzhou; Prince Ying of Linchuan was made commander over nine provinces including Jing and Yong and inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏尚書令王睿進爵中山王，加鎮東大將軍；

translations.literal: That year, Wei's Director of the Affairs of Masters of Writing Wang Rui was advanced to Prince of Zhongshan and promoted to Grand General Who Guards the East;
translations.idiomatic: That year Wei's director of the masters of writing, Wang Rui, was enfeoffed as prince of Zhongshan and made grand general who guards the east;

sentences.zh: 置王官二十二人，以中書侍郎鄭羲爲傅，郎中令以下皆當時名士。

translations.literal: Twenty-two princely officials were appointed; Secretariat Gentleman Zheng Xi was made tutor, and all ranks from Chief of Palace Attendants downward were celebrated men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: twenty-two princely household officers were appointed, with Zheng Xi as tutor and every post from chief of palace attendants down filled by celebrated men.

sentences.zh: 又拜睿妻丁氏爲妃。

translations.literal: Rui's wife, Lady Ding, was also enfeoffed as princess consort.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ding, Rui's wife, was also enfeoffed as princess consort.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，封皇子鋒爲江夏王。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the emperor's son Feng was enfeoffed as Prince of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring the emperor enfeoffed his son Feng as prince of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 魏人寇淮陽，圍軍主成買於甬城，上遣領軍將軍李安民爲都督，與軍主周盤龍等救之。

translations.literal: Wei forces raided Huaiyang and besieged the garrison commander Cheng Mai at Yongcheng; the emperor sent General of the Palace Guard Li Anmin as commander, together with garrison commander Zhou Panlong and others, to relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei raided Huaiyang and besieged Cheng Mai at Yongcheng; the emperor sent Li Anmin, general of the palace guard, as commander with Zhou Panlong and others to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 魏人緣淮大掠，江北民皆驚走，渡江，成買力戰而死。

translations.literal: Wei forces looted heavily along the Huai; north-bank civilians fled in panic across the river. Cheng Mai fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Wei forces plundered the Huai line; civilians north of the river fled in terror across the water while Cheng Mai fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 盤龍之子奉叔以二百人陷陳深入，魏以萬餘騎張左右翼圍之。

translations.literal: Panlong's son Fengshu plunged deep into the enemy lines with two hundred men; Wei deployed more than ten thousand horsemen in wings to encircle them.
translations.idiomatic: Panlong's son Fengshu drove two hundred men deep into the Wei lines; Wei answered with more than ten thousand horsemen spreading wings to surround them.

sentences.zh: 或告盤龍云「奉叔已沒」，盤龍馳馬奮槊，直突魏陳，所向披靡。

translations.literal: Someone told Panlong that Fengshu had been killed; Panlong spurred his horse and brandished his spear, charging straight through the Wei battle line, scattering all before him.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached Panlong that Fengshu had fallen, he spurred his horse, levelled his spear, and charged straight through the Wei formation, scattering all before him.

sentences.zh: 奉叔已出，復入求盤龍。

translations.literal: Fengshu had already broken out but reentered the fray looking for Panlong.
translations.idiomatic: Fengshu had already broken free but turned back into the fight searching for his father.

sentences.zh: 父子兩騎縈擾，魏數萬之眾莫敢當者；

translations.literal: Father and son, two riders weaving through the field—none among Wei's tens of thousands dared stand against them;
translations.idiomatic: The two riders, father and son, wheeled through the field, and none among Wei's tens of thousands dared stand against them;

sentences.zh: 魏師遂敗，殺傷萬計。

translations.literal: The Wei army was routed; casualties numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army broke; killed and wounded numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 魏師退，李安民等引兵追之，戰於孫溪渚，又破之。

translations.literal: As the Wei army withdrew, Li Anmin and others pursued and again defeated them at Sunxi Islet.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei army retreated, Li Anmin pursued and defeated them again at Sunxi Islet.

sentences.zh: 己卯，魏主南巡，司空苟頹留守；

translations.literal: On jimao, the Wei emperor made a southern tour; Minister of Works Gou Ti remained to govern;
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the Wei emperor toured south, leaving Minister of Works Gou Ti to govern;

sentences.zh: 丁亥，魏主至中山。

translations.literal: On dinghai the Wei emperor reached Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai he reached Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛卯朔，魏大赦。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the xinmao day, new moon, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: At the second month's new moon on xinmao, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，游擊將軍桓康覆敗魏師於淮陽，進攻樊諧城，拔之。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Swift-Cavalry General Huan Kang totally defeated Wei forces at Huaiyang, then attacked and took Fanyu City.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou Swift-Cavalry General Huan Kang crushed Wei at Huaiyang and took Fanyu City.

sentences.zh: 魏主自中山如信都；

translations.literal: The Wei emperor went from Zhongshan to Xindu;
translations.idiomatic: From Zhongshan the Wei emperor went on to Xindu;

sentences.zh: 癸卯，復如中山；

translations.literal: On guimao he returned to Zhongshan;
translations.idiomatic: On guimao he went back to Zhongshan;

sentences.zh: 庚戌，還，至肆州。

translations.literal: On gengxu he headed back and reached Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu he turned back and reached Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 沙門法秀以妖術惑眾，謀作亂於平城；

translations.literal: The monk Faxiu used sorcery to mislead the people and plotted rebellion at Pingcheng;
translations.idiomatic: The monk Faxiu used sorcery to beguile the people and plotted rebellion at Pingcheng;

sentences.zh: 苟頹帥禁兵收掩，悉擒之。

translations.literal: Gou Ti led the palace guard in a roundup and seized them all.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Ti led the palace guard in a roundup and took them all.

sentences.zh: 魏主還平城，有司囚法秀，加以籠頭，鐵鎖無故自解。

translations.literal: When the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng, the authorities imprisoned Faxiu, fitted him with a cangue, and his iron chains inexplicably came loose on their own.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng, Faxiu was imprisoned and fitted with a cangue, yet his iron chains came loose of themselves.

sentences.zh: 魏人穿其頸骨，祝之曰：「若果有神，當令穿肉不入。」

translations.literal: The Wei people pierced his neck bone and prayed: "If he truly has divine power, let the piercing not enter the flesh.
translations.idiomatic: They pierced his neck bone and prayed, "If he truly has divine power, let the iron not bite into the flesh."

sentences.zh: 遂穿以徇，三日乃死。

translations.literal: They pierced him through for public display; after three days he died.
translations.idiomatic: They ran him through for public display, and after three days he died.

sentences.zh: 議者或欲盡殺道人，馮太后不可，乃止。

translations.literal: Some in council wished to slaughter all monks; Empress Dowager Feng would not allow it, and the proposal was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged killing every monk, but Empress Dowager Feng forbade it and the matter ended.

sentences.zh: 垣崇祖之敗魏師也，恐魏復寇淮北，乃徙下蔡戍於淮東。

translations.literal: After Yuan Chongzu's defeat of Wei, fearing a renewed Wei raid on north Huai, he moved the Xiakai garrison east of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Chongzu defeated Wei, fearing another raid on the north Huai he moved the Xiakai garrison east of the river.

sentences.zh: 既而魏師果至，欲攻下蔡；

translations.literal: Before long Wei forces did arrive and intended to attack Xiakai;
translations.idiomatic: Wei forces soon arrived intending to strike Xiakai;

sentences.zh: 聞其內徙，欲夷其故城。

translations.literal: Learning the garrison had been withdrawn inward, they meant to raze the old fort.
translations.idiomatic: Learning the post had been withdrawn, they meant to raze the old fort.

sentences.zh: 己酉，崇祖引兵渡淮擊魏，大破之，殺獲千計。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Chongzu crossed the Huai with troops and struck Wei, routing them with more than a thousand killed or captured.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Chongzu crossed the Huai and routed Wei, killing or capturing more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 晉、宋之際，荊州刺史多不領南蠻校尉，別以重人居之。

translations.literal: Between Jin and Song, the Inspector of Jingzhou often did not hold the post of Colonel of the Southern Man; a separate heavyweight was usually assigned to it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin and Song the inspector of Jingzhou often did not hold the southern Man colonelcy; a separate senior officer usually did.

sentences.zh: 豫章王嶷爲荊、湘二州刺史，領南蠻。

translations.literal: Prince of Yuzhang Liao served as Inspector of Jing and Xiang, holding also the Southern Man colonelcy.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liao of Yuzhang had served as inspector of Jing and Xiang while also holding the southern Man colonelcy.

sentences.zh: 嶷罷，更以侍中王奐爲之，奐固辭，曰：「西土戎燼之後，痍毀難復。

translations.literal: When Liao was relieved, Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Huan was appointed in his place; Huan firmly declined, saying: "After the western regions were scorched by warfare, the devastation cannot quickly be repaired.
translations.idiomatic: When Liao was relieved, Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Huan was named to succeed him; Huan firmly declined, saying, "The west has been burned by war and cannot quickly be rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 今復割撤太府，制置偏校，崇望不足助強，語實交能相弊。

translations.literal: To carve away and remove the grand prefecture again and set up a separate subordinate command adds prestige without real strength and in practice only makes the two offices interfere with each other.
translations.idiomatic: To split off the grand prefecture again and set up a separate subordinate command adds title without strength and in practice only lets the two offices work against each other.

sentences.zh: 且資力既分，職司增廣，眾勞務倍，文案滋煩，竊以爲國計非允。」

translations.literal: Moreover, once resources and manpower are divided, duties multiply, popular labor doubles, and paperwork grows more burdensome—this, I submit, does not serve the state's interest.
translations.idiomatic: Once resources and manpower are divided, duties multiply, labor doubles, and paperwork swells—I submit this does not serve the state.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，罷南蠻校尉官。

translations.literal: On guichou the office of Colonel of the Southern Man was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou the southern Man colonelcy was abolished.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛酉朔，魏主如肆州；

translations.literal: In the third month, on the xinyou day, new moon, the Wei emperor went to Sizhou;
translations.idiomatic: At the third month's new moon on xinyou the Wei emperor went to Sizhou;

sentences.zh: 己巳，還平城。

translations.literal: On jisi he returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi he was back at Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 魏法秀之亂，事連蘭台御史張求等百餘人，皆以反，法當族。

translations.literal: In the Wei Faxiu affair, more than a hundred people were implicated including Palace Archivist Censor Zhang Qiu; all were charged with rebellion and liable by law to execution of the whole clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Faxiu affair more than a hundred people, including palace archivist censor Zhang Qiu, were implicated; all were charged with rebellion and liable to clan execution.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王睿請誅首惡，宥其餘黨。

translations.literal: Director of the Affairs of Masters of Writing Wang Rui asked to execute the ringleaders and spare the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the masters of writing Wang Rui asked to execute the ringleaders and spare the rest.

sentences.zh: 乃詔：「應誅五族者，降爲三族；

translations.literal: An edict was issued: "Where execution of five clans is prescribed, reduce it to three;
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "Where five clans are to be executed, reduce the sentence to three;

sentences.zh: 三族者，門誅；

translations.literal: where three clans are prescribed, reduce it to execution of the household at the gate;
translations.idiomatic: where three clans are prescribed, reduce it to execution of the offender's household at the gate;

sentences.zh: 門誅，止其身。」

translations.literal: for household execution, apply only to the offender himself."
translations.idiomatic: and for household execution, apply the penalty only to the offender himself."

sentences.zh: 所免千餘人。

translations.literal: More than a thousand persons were spared thereby.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand people were spared.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己亥，魏主如方山。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jihai, the Wei emperor went to Fangshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on jihai, the Wei emperor went to Fangshan.

sentences.zh: 馮太后樂其山川，曰：「它日必葬我於是，不必祔山陵也。」

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Feng delighted in its mountains and waters and said: "One day bury me here; there is no need to join the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Feng delighted in its mountains and waters and said, "Bury me here one day; there is no need to join the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 乃爲太后作壽陵，又建永固石室於山上，欲以爲廟。

translations.literal: A longevity tomb was built for the empress dowager, and on the mountain the Eternal Firmness stone hall was erected, intended as a shrine.
translations.idiomatic: A longevity tomb was built for her, and on the mountain the Eternal Firmness stone hall was raised as a shrine.

sentences.zh: 桓標之等有眾數萬，寨險求援；

translations.literal: Huan Biaozhi and others had a force of tens of thousands, holding fortified positions and seeking relief;
translations.idiomatic: Huan Biaozhi and others, tens of thousands strong, held fortified positions and sought relief;

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔李安民督諸將往迎之，又使兗州刺史周山圖自淮入清，倍道應接。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Li Anmin was ordered to lead the generals to meet them; Inspector of Yanzhou Zhou Shantu was also sent from the Huai into the Qing River by forced march to link up.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Li Anmin was ordered to lead the generals to meet them, and Inspector of Yanzhou Zhou Shantu was sent from the Huai into the Qing by forced march to link up.

sentences.zh: 淮北民桓磊磈破魏師於抱犢固。

translations.literal: Huan Leikui, a man of north Huai, defeated Wei forces at Baodugu.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Leikui of north Huai defeated Wei at Baodugu.

sentences.zh: 李安民赴救遲留，標之等皆爲魏所滅，餘眾得南歸者尚數千家；

translations.literal: Li Anmin's relief arrived too late; Biaozhi and the rest were all destroyed by Wei, though several thousand households among the survivors reached the south;
translations.idiomatic: Li Anmin arrived too late; Biaozhi and the rest were destroyed by Wei, though several thousand households among the survivors reached the south;

sentences.zh: 魏人亦掠三萬餘口歸平城。

translations.literal: Wei forces also carried off more than thirty thousand captives back to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wei also carried more than thirty thousand captives back to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 魏任城康王雲卒。

translations.literal: Prince Kang of Rencheng Yun of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang of Rencheng, Yun of Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬戌，鄧至王像舒遣使入貢於魏。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on renxu, King Xiangshu of Dengzhi sent envoys bearing tribute to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renxu, King Xiangshu of Dengzhi sent envoys with tribute to Wei.

sentences.zh: 鄧至者，羌之別種，國於宕昌之南。

translations.literal: The Dengzhi were a separate branch of the Qiang, with their state south of Dangchang.
translations.idiomatic: The Dengzhi were a Qiang offshoot whose state lay south of Dangchang.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬子，大赦。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on renzi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renzi, the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，魏中山宣王王睿卒。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Prince Xuan of Zhongshan Wang Rui of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Prince Xuan of Zhongshan, Wang Rui of Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 睿疾病，太皇太后、魏主累至其家視疾。

translations.literal: When Rui fell ill, the grand empress dowager and the Wei emperor repeatedly visited his home to attend him.
translations.idiomatic: When Rui fell ill, the grand empress dowager and the Wei emperor repeatedly visited his home.

sentences.zh: 及卒，贈太宰，立廟於平城南。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously made Grand Mentor, and a temple was established south of Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made grand mentor, and a temple was established south of Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 文士爲睿作哀詩及言耒者百餘人，及葬，自稱親姻、義舊，縗絰哭送者千餘人。

translations.literal: More than a hundred literati composed elegies for Rui and laudatory writings; at the burial, more than a thousand who declared themselves kin by marriage or old friends in mourning dress followed weeping.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred literati wrote elegies and dirges for him; at the burial more than a thousand who called themselves kin by marriage or old friends followed in mourning dress, weeping.

sentences.zh: 魏主以睿子中散大夫襲代睿爲尚書令，領吏部曹。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor had Rui's son Xi, Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Library, succeed Rui as Director of the Affairs of Masters of Writing, overseeing the Department of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor had Rui's son Xi, a gentleman attendant at the palace library, succeed him as director of the masters of writing, overseeing personnel.

sentences.zh: 戊午，魏封皇叔簡爲齊郡王，猛爲安豐王。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Wei enfeoffed the emperor's uncle Jian as Prince of Qijun and Meng as Prince of Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Wei enfeoffed the emperor's uncle Jian as prince of Qijun and Meng as prince of Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己未朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the jiwei day, new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: At the seventh month's new moon on jiwei there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 上使後軍參軍車僧朗使於魏。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Rear Army Attendant Che Senglang as envoy to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Rear Army Attendant Che Senglang as envoy to Wei.

sentences.zh: 甲子，僧朗至平城，魏主問曰：「齊輔宋日淺，何故遽登大位？」

translations.literal: On jiazi, Senglang reached Pingcheng. The Wei emperor asked: "Qi assisted Song for only a short time—why did you suddenly ascend the throne?
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Senglang reached Pingcheng. The Wei emperor asked, "Qi assisted Song for so brief a time—why did you suddenly take the throne?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「虞、夏登庸，身陟元後，魏、晉匡輔，貽厥子孫，時宜各異耳。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Yu and Xia rose by promotion and ascended to supreme sovereignty themselves; Wei and Jin assisted others and bequeathed power to their descendants—each age had its proper time.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Yu and Xia rose by promotion and took the throne themselves; Wei and Jin assisted others and bequeathed power to their descendants—each age has its proper way.

translations.literal: Closing quotation.
translations.idiomatic: Closing quotation.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，柔然別帥他稽帥眾降魏。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Taji, a separate chief of Rouran, led his followers in surrender to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Taji, a separate Rouran chief, led his followers in surrender to Wei.

sentences.zh: 楊文弘遣使請降，詔復以爲北秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Yang Wenhong sent envoys requesting surrender; an edict restored him as Inspector of North Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wenhong sent envoys requesting surrender, and an edict restored him as inspector of North Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，楊廣香卒，其眾半奔文弘，半奔梁州。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang Guangxiang had died; half his followers fled to Wenhong, half to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yang Guangxiang had died; half his followers fled to Wenhong, half to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 文弘遣楊後起據白水。

translations.literal: Wenhong sent Yang Houqi to hold Baishui.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhong sent Yang Houqi to occupy Baishui.

sentences.zh: 上雖授以官爵，而陰敕晉壽太守楊公則使伺便圖之。

translations.literal: Though the emperor invested him with office and rank, he secretly ordered Jinshou Administrator Yang Gongze to watch for a chance to destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor invested him with office and rank, he secretly ordered Yang Gongze, administrator of Jinshou, to watch for a chance to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 宋升明中，遣使者殷靈誕、苟昭先如魏，聞上受禪，靈誕謂魏典客曰：「宋、魏通好，憂患是同。

translations.literal: During Song's Shengming era, envoys Yin Lingdan and Gou Zhaoxian were sent to Wei; learning the emperor had received the abdication, Lingdan told Wei's Director of Guests: "Song and Wei were on friendly terms and shared the same anxieties.
translations.idiomatic: During Song's Shengming era envoys Yin Lingdan and Gou Zhaoxian were sent to Wei; when they learned the emperor had received the abdication, Lingdan told Wei's director of guests, "Song and Wei were allies and shared the same anxieties.

sentences.zh: 宋今滅亡，魏不相救，何用和親！」

translations.literal: Song is now destroyed and Wei did not come to its aid—what use is alliance by marriage!"
translations.idiomatic: Song is destroyed and Wei did not rescue it—what use is alliance by marriage!"

sentences.zh: 及劉昶入寇，靈誕請爲昶司馬，不許。

translations.literal: When Liu Chang invaded, Lingdan asked to serve as Chang's chief of staff but was refused.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chang invaded, Lingdan asked to serve as his chief of staff but was refused.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚午，魏閱武於南郊，因宴群臣，置車僧朗於靈誕下，僧朗不肯就席，曰：「靈誕昔爲宋使，今爲齊民。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on gengwu, Wei reviewed troops at the southern suburb and then feasted his ministers, seating Che Senglang below Lingdan. Senglang refused to take his seat and said: "Lingdan was once Song's envoy; he is now a subject of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on gengwu, Wei reviewed troops at the southern suburb and feasted the court, seating Che Senglang below Lingdan. Senglang refused his seat and said, "Lingdan was once Song's envoy; he is now a subject of Qi.

sentences.zh: 乞魏主以禮見處。」

translations.literal: I ask that the Wei emperor treat us according to proper ritual.
translations.idiomatic: I ask the Wei emperor to seat us according to proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 靈誕遂與相忿詈。

translations.literal: Lingdan and he then exchanged angry curses.
translations.idiomatic: Lingdan and he then cursed each other in fury.

sentences.zh: 劉昶賂宋降人解奉君於會刺殺僧朗，魏人收奉君，誅之；

translations.literal: Liu Chang bribed the Song defector Xie Fengjun to assassinate Senglang at the gathering; Wei authorities seized Fengjun and executed him;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang bribed the Song defector Xie Fengjun to assassinate Senglang at the gathering; Wei seized Fengjun and executed him;

sentences.zh: 厚送僧朗之喪，放靈誕等南歸。

translations.literal: Senglang's body was sent back with full honors, and Lingdan and the others were released to return south.
translations.idiomatic: Senglang's body was sent back with full honors, and Lingdan and the rest were released to return south.

sentences.zh: 及世祖即位，昭先具以靈誕之語啟聞，靈誕坐下獄死。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Zhaoxian reported Lingdan's words in full; Lingdan was imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu took the throne, Zhaoxian reported Lingdan's words in full, and Lingdan was imprisoned and died.

sentences.zh: 辛未，柔然主遣使來聘，與上書，謂上爲「足下」，自稱曰「吾」，遣上師子皮褲褶，約共伐魏。

translations.literal: On xinwei, the Rouran ruler sent envoys on a friendly mission and wrote a letter addressing the emperor as "below your feet," calling himself "I," sending a lion-skin jacket and trousers, and proposing a joint campaign against Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei the Rouran ruler sent envoys and wrote addressing the emperor as "below your feet," calling himself "I," sending a lion-skin jacket and trousers and proposing a joint campaign against Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏尉元、薛虎子克五固，斬司馬朗之，東南諸州皆平。

translations.literal: Wei's Yu Yuan and Xue Huzi captured Wugu, beheaded Sima Langzhi, and the southeastern provinces were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Yu Yuan and Xue Huzi captured Wugu, beheaded Sima Langzhi, and pacified the southeastern provinces.

sentences.zh: 尉元入爲侍中、都曹尚書，薛虎子爲彭城鎮將，遷徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Yu Yuan entered court as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Central Secretariat; Xue Huzi became garrison general of Pengcheng and was transferred to Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yuan entered court as attendant-in-ordinary and director of the central secretariat; Xue Huzi became garrison general of Pengcheng and was transferred to inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時州鎮戍兵，資絹自隨，不入公庫。

translations.literal: At this time garrison troops of provinces and commanderies carried their own silk rations and did not deposit them in the public storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: At this time provincial and garrison troops carried their own silk rations and did not deposit them in the public storehouse.

sentences.zh: 虎子上表，以爲：「國家欲取江東，先須積穀彭城。

translations.literal: Huzi submitted a memorial, stating: "If the state intends to take the lands east of the Yangtze, it must first accumulate grain at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huzi submitted a memorial: "If the state intends to take the lands east of the Yangtze, it must first accumulate grain at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 切惟在鎮之兵，不減數萬，資糧之絹，人十二匹；

translations.literal: Considering carefully: troops stationed at the garrison number no fewer than tens of thousands; each man's ration in silk is twelve bolts;
translations.idiomatic: The garrison holds no fewer than tens of thousands of men; each man's ration is twelve bolts of silk;

sentences.zh: 用度無准，未及代下，不免饑寒，公私損費。

translations.literal: expenditures have no fixed standard, and before rotations replace them they cannot avoid hunger and cold—waste for both public and private funds.
translations.idiomatic: expenditures have no fixed standard, and before reliefs arrive the men cannot avoid hunger and cold—waste for public and private alike.

sentences.zh: 今徐州良田十萬餘頃，水陸肥沃，清、汴通流，足以溉灌。

translations.literal: Now Xuzhou has more than a hundred thousand qing of fine farmland, fertile by land and water; the Qing and Bian rivers flow through it, enough for irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou has more than a hundred thousand qing of fine farmland, fertile by land and water; the Qing and Bian rivers flow through it and can irrigate.

sentences.zh: 若以兵絹市牛，可得萬頭，興置屯田，一歲之中，且給官食。

translations.literal: If the troops' silk were used to buy oxen, ten thousand head could be obtained; establish military colonies, and within one year the court could supply its own grain.
translations.idiomatic: If the troops' silk were used to buy oxen, ten thousand head could be obtained; establish military colonies, and within one year the court could feed itself.

sentences.zh: 半兵芸殖，餘兵屯戍，且耕且守，不妨捍邊。

translations.literal: Half the soldiers would till and plant, the rest garrison and defend—farming and guarding at once without hindering frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: Half the soldiers would till and plant, the rest garrison and defend—farming and guarding at once without weakening the frontier.

sentences.zh: 一年之收，過於十倍之絹；

translations.literal: One year's harvest would exceed ten times the value of the silk ration;
translations.idiomatic: A single year's harvest would be worth more than ten years of silk rations;

sentences.zh: 暫時之耕，足充數載之食。

translations.literal: Temporary tillage would suffice to fill several years' food.
translations.idiomatic: A season's planting would supply food for several years.

sentences.zh: 於後兵資皆貯公庫，五稔之後，谷帛俱溢，非直戍卒豐飽，亦有吞敵之勢。」

translations.literal: Thereafter all military supplies would be stored in the public granaries; after five harvests grain and cloth would both overflow—not only would garrison soldiers be full and fed, there would also be the momentum to swallow the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter all military supplies would go into public storehouses; after five harvests grain and cloth would overflow—not only would the garrison troops eat their fill, but the state would also gain the strength to overwhelm its foes.

sentences.zh: 魏人從之。

translations.literal: The Wei people followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei court adopted the plan.

sentences.zh: 虎子爲政有惠愛，兵民懷之。

translations.literal: Huzi in governing had kindness and care; soldiers and people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: Huzi governed with kindness and compassion, and soldiers and civilians alike held him in affection.

sentences.zh: 會沛郡太守邵安、下邳太守張攀以贓污爲虎子所案，各遣子上書，告虎子與江南通，魏主曰：「虎子必不然。」

translations.literal: It happened that Shao An, prefect of Pei Commandery, and Zhang Pan, prefect of Xiapi, were investigated by Huzi for corruption; each sent his son to submit a memorial accusing Huzi of communicating with the lands south of the Yangtze. The Wei ruler said: "Huzi surely is not so.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao An, prefect of Pei, and Zhang Pan, prefect of Xiapi, were investigated by Huzi for corruption, each sent his son to memorial the throne, accusing Huzi of colluding with the Southern dynasties. The Wei emperor said, "Huzi would never do such a thing.

sentences.zh: 推按，果虛，詔安、攀皆賜死，二子各鞭一百。

translations.literal: Upon investigation it proved false; an edict ordered both An and Pan granted death, and each son flogged one hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: An investigation found the charges baseless. An and Pan were both ordered to take their own lives, and each son was flogged one hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾王拾寅卒，世子度易侯立。

translations.literal: Shibin, king of Tuyuhun, died; his heir Duyihou succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Shibin, king of Tuyuhun, died, and his heir Duyihou succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊子朔，以度易侯爲西秦、河二州刺史、河南王。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day wuzi, Duyihou was made Governor of the two provinces of Western Qin and He and Prince of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day of the cycle (wuzi), Duyihou was appointed governor of Western Qin and He provinces and enfeoffed as Prince of Henan.

sentences.zh: 魏中書令高閭等更定新律成，凡八百三十二章；

translations.literal: Gao Lu, Wei Director of the Secretariat, and others completed the revision of the new code, eight hundred thirty-two articles in all;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lu, Director of the Secretariat of Wei, and others completed the revision of the new legal code—eight hundred thirty-two articles in all;

sentences.zh: 門房之誅十有六，大辟二百三十五，雜刑三百七十七。

translations.literal: clan-extinction punishments sixteen, capital offenses two hundred thirty-five, miscellaneous penalties three hundred seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: sixteen articles on clan-extinction punishments, two hundred thirty-five capital offenses, and three hundred seventy-seven miscellaneous penalties.

sentences.zh: 初，高昌王闞伯周卒，子義成立；

translations.literal: Earlier, Kan Bozhou, king of Gaochang, died, and his son Yicheng succeeded;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Kan Bozhou, king of Gaochang, had died, and his son Yicheng succeeded him;

sentences.zh: 是歲，其從兄首歸殺義成自立。

translations.literal: That year his older cousin Shougui killed Yicheng and set himself up.
translations.idiomatic: That year his older cousin Shougui killed Yicheng and seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 高車王可至羅殺首歸兄弟，以敦煌張明爲高昌王。

translations.literal: Kezhiluo, king of the Gaoche, killed Shougui and his brothers and installed Zhang Ming of Dunhuang as king of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: Kezhiluo, king of the Gaoche, killed Shougui and his brothers and installed Zhang Ming of Dunhuang as king of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 國人殺明，立馬儒爲王。

translations.literal: The people of the state killed Ming and installed Ma Ru as king.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Gaochang killed Ming and enthroned Ma Ru as king.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬戌，詔置學生二百人，以中書令張緒爲國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on renxu, an edict established two hundred students and made Zhang Xu, Director of the Secretariat, Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on renxu, an edict enrolled two hundred students at the Imperial Academy and appointed Zhang Xu, Director of the Secretariat, as its director.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，魏大赦。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Wei granted a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚申，上召司徒褚淵、尚書左僕射王儉受遺詔輔太子；

translations.literal: In the third month, on gengshen, the Emperor summoned Minister over the Masses Chu Yuan and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Jian to receive the deathbed edict and assist the Crown Prince;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengshen, the Emperor summoned Minister over the Masses Chu Yuan and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Jian to receive his deathbed edict and assist the Crown Prince;

sentences.zh: 壬戌，殂於臨光殿。

translations.literal: On renxu, he died in the Lin'guang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, he died in the Lin'guang Hall.

sentences.zh: 太子即位，大赦。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince ascended the throne and granted a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince ascended the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 高帝沉深有大量，博學能文。

translations.literal: The High Emperor was deep and reserved with great capacity, broadly learned and able in letters.
translations.idiomatic: The High Emperor was deep and reserved, possessed of great forbearance, broadly learned, and skilled in letters.

sentences.zh: 性清儉，主衣中有玉導，上敕中書曰：「留此正是興長病源！」

translations.literal: By nature he was pure and frugal; in the wardrobe office there was a jade belt guide. The Emperor ordered the Secretariat, saying: "Keeping this is precisely to raise up a long-lasting source of illness!"
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was austere and frugal. In the wardrobe office he found a jade belt clasp and ordered the Secretariat: "Keeping such things is exactly how one breeds lasting corruption!"

sentences.zh: 即命擊碎；

translations.literal: He at once ordered it smashed;
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered it smashed;

sentences.zh: 仍案檢有何異物，皆隨此例。

translations.literal: then had an inventory made of what other unusual objects there were, and all were treated by this precedent.
translations.idiomatic: then had the wardrobe searched for other luxuries, all of which were destroyed in the same way.

sentences.zh: 每曰：「使我治天下十年，當使黃金與土同價。」

translations.literal: He often said: "If I were to govern the realm for ten years, I would make gold the same price as earth."
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "Give me ten years to govern the realm, and I will make gold worth no more than dirt."

sentences.zh: 乙丑，以褚淵錄尚書事，王儉爲侍中、尚書令，車騎將軍張敬兒開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On yichou, Chu Yuan was made Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing; Wang Jian was made Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat; General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang Jinger was given the Grand General's Staff with Protocol Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Chu Yuan was appointed to oversee the Secretariat; Wang Jian became Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat; and General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang Jinger was granted a grand general's staff with protocol equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以前將軍王奐爲尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: On dingmao, former General Wang Huan was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, former General Wang Huan was appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以豫章王嶷爲太尉。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Prince Yi of Yuzhang was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Prince Yi of Yuzhang was appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，魏主臨虎圈，詔曰：「虎狼猛暴，取捕之日，每多傷害；

translations.literal: On gengchen, the Wei ruler visited the tiger enclosure and issued an edict, saying: "Tigers and wolves are fierce and savage; on the days they are captured many are injured;
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, the Wei emperor visited the tiger park and issued an edict: "Tigers and wolves are fierce and savage, and capturing them often injures many men;

sentences.zh: 既無所益，損費良多，從今勿復捕貢。」

translations.literal: since they bring no benefit and the waste and expense are great, from now on do not again capture and present them as tribute."
translations.idiomatic: they serve no useful purpose and the cost is great. Henceforth, do not capture them for tribute."

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚寅，上大行謚曰高皇帝，廟號太祖。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on gengyin, the late Emperor was given the posthumous title High Emperor and the temple name Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on gengyin, the late emperor was given the posthumous title High Emperor and the temple name Taizu.

sentences.zh: 丙午，葬泰安陵。

translations.literal: On bingwu, he was buried at Tai'an Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, he was buried at Tai'an Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，追尊穆妃爲皇后。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Consort Mu was posthumously honored as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Consort Mu was posthumously honored as empress.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲申朔，立南郡王長懋爲皇太子。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the first day jiashen, Prince Changmao of Nanjun was established as Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the first day of the cycle (jiashen), Prince Changmao of Nanjun was installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 丙申，立太子妃王氏。

translations.literal: On bingshen, the Crown Prince's consort, Lady Wang, was established.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Lady Wang was installed as crown princess.

sentences.zh: 妃，琅邪人也。

translations.literal: The consort was a native of Langya.
translations.idiomatic: The crown princess was a native of Langya.

sentences.zh: 封皇子聞喜公子良爲竟陵王，臨汝公子卿爲廬陵王，應城公子敬爲安陸王，江陵公子懋爲晉安王，枝江公子隆爲隨郡王，子真爲建安王，皇孫昭業爲南郡王。

translations.literal: The princes were enfeoffed: Ziliang, son of the Prince of Wenxi, as Prince of Jingling; Ziqing, son of the Prince of Linru, as Prince of Luling; Zijing, son of the Prince of Yingcheng, as Prince of Anlu; Zimao, son of the Prince of Jiangling, as Prince of Jin'an; Zilong, son of the Prince of Zhijiang, as Prince of Suijun; Zizhen as Prince of Jian'an; and the imperial grandson Zhaoye as Prince of Nanjun.
translations.idiomatic: Princes were enfeoffed: Ziliang, son of the Prince of Wenxi, as Prince of Jingling; Ziqing, son of the Prince of Linru, as Prince of Luling; Zijing, son of the Prince of Yingcheng, as Prince of Anlu; Zimao, son of the Prince of Jiangling, as Prince of Jin'an; Zilong, son of the Prince of Zhijiang, as Prince of Suijun; Zizhen as Prince of Jian'an; and the imperial grandson Zhaoye as Prince of Nanjun.

sentences.zh: 司徒褚淵寢疾，自表遜位，世祖不許，淵固請懇切，癸卯，以淵爲司空，領驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Chu Yuan lay ill in bed and submitted a memorial yielding his post; Emperor Shizu did not permit it, but Yuan urgently and earnestly pleaded. On guimao, Yuan was made Minister of Works and concurrently General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Chu Yuan fell gravely ill and memorialized to resign; Emperor Shizu refused, but Yuan pleaded earnestly. On guimao, he was made Minister of Works and concurrently General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 侍中、錄尚書如故。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He retained his posts as Palace Attendant and overseer of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，魏發州郡五萬人治靈丘道。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Wei mobilized fifty thousand men from the provinces and commanderies to repair the Lingqiu road.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Wei mobilized fifty thousand men from the provinces and commanderies to repair the Lingqiu road.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書濟陽江謐，性諂躁，太祖殂，謐恨不豫顧命；

translations.literal: Jiang Mi of Jiyang, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, was by nature fawning and restless; when Taizu died, Mi resented that he had not been included in the final testament;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Mi of Jiyang, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, was fawning and impetuous by nature. When Taizu died, Mi resented being left out of the deathbed testament;

sentences.zh: 上即位，謐又不遷官；

translations.literal: when the Emperor ascended the throne, Mi was again not promoted;
translations.idiomatic: when the new emperor took the throne, Mi was passed over for promotion again;

sentences.zh: 以此怨望、誹謗。

translations.literal: because of this he harbored resentment and slandered.
translations.idiomatic: and he nursed resentment and spread slander.

sentences.zh: 會上不豫，謐詣豫章王嶷請問，曰：「至尊非起疾東宮又非才，公今欲作何計？」

translations.literal: It happened that the Emperor was ill; Mi went to Prince Yi of Yuzhang to inquire, saying: "The Sovereign is gravely ill, and the heir in the Eastern Palace lacks talent—what plan does Your Highness intend now?"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, Mi went to Prince Yi of Yuzhang and asked, "The sovereign is gravely ill, and the heir in the Eastern Palace lacks ability—what does Your Highness intend to do?"

sentences.zh: 上知雲，使御史中丞沈沖奏謐前後罪惡，庚寅，賜謐死。

translations.literal: The Emperor learned of it and had Censor-in-Chief Shen Chong memorialize Mi's crimes past and present; on gengyin, Mi was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor learned of this and had Censor-in-Chief Shen Chong memorialize Mi's crimes. On gengyin, Mi was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，南康文簡公褚淵卒，世子侍中賁恥其父失節，服除，遂不仕，以爵讓其弟蓁，屏居墓下終身。

translations.literal: On guimao, Wenjian Duke of Nankang Chu Yuan died. His heir, Palace Attendant Ben, was ashamed that his father had lost integrity; when mourning ended he would not take office, yielded his title to his younger brother Zhen, and lived in seclusion by the tomb for life.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Wenjian Duke of Nankang Chu Yuan died. His heir Ben, a palace attendant, was ashamed that his father had compromised himself during the dynastic transition; when mourning ended he refused office, ceded his title to his younger brother Zhen, and lived out his days in seclusion beside the tomb.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁巳，以國哀罷國子學。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on dingsi, because of national mourning the Imperial Academy was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on dingsi, the Imperial Academy was closed for national mourning.

sentences.zh: 氐王楊文弘卒。

translations.literal: Wenhong, king of the Di, died.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhong, king of the Di, died.

sentences.zh: 諸子皆幼，乃以兄子後起爲嗣。

translations.literal: All his sons were young, so his elder brother's son Houqi was made successor.
translations.idiomatic: All his sons were still young, so he named his elder brother's son Houqi as his successor.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛酉，魏以後起爲武都王，文弘子集始爲白水太守。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on xinyou, Wei made Houqi Prince of Wudu and Wenhong's son Jishi Prefect of Baishui.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinyou, Wei enfeoffed Houqi as Prince of Wudu and appointed Wenhong's son Jishi prefect of Baishui.

sentences.zh: 既而集始自立爲王，後起擊破之。

translations.literal: Soon after, Jishi set himself up as king; Houqi defeated and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Jishi declared himself king, but Houqi defeated him.

sentences.zh: 魏以荊州巴、氐擾亂，以鎮西大將軍李崇爲荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Because the Ba and Di in Jing Province were in turmoil, Wei made Grand General Who Guards the West Li Chong Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Ba and Di peoples in Jing Province were in revolt, Wei appointed Grand General Who Guards the West Li Chong governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 崇，顯祖之舅子也。

translations.literal: Chong was a nephew by marriage of Emperor Xianzu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong was a nephew by marriage of Emperor Xianzu.

sentences.zh: 將之鎮，敕發陝、秦二州兵送之，崇辭曰：「邊人失和，本怨刺史。

translations.literal: As he was about to go to his post, an edict ordered troops from Shaan and Qin provinces to escort him. Chong declined, saying: "The frontier people have lost harmony; their resentment was originally against the governor.
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to take up his post, an edict ordered troops from Shaan and Qin provinces to escort him. Li Chong declined, saying, "The frontier peoples are unsettled because they resented the previous governor.

sentences.zh: 今奉詔代之，自然安靖；

translations.literal: Now that I come by imperial order to replace him, they will naturally be settled;
translations.idiomatic: Now that I come by imperial order to replace him, they will naturally be pacified;

sentences.zh: 但須一詔而已，不煩發兵自防，使之懷懼也。」

translations.literal: only one edict is needed—there is no need to trouble sending troops to guard myself and make them harbor fear."
translations.idiomatic: an edict alone will suffice. There is no need to send troops to protect me and frighten them further."

sentences.zh: 魏朝從之。

translations.literal: The Wei court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei court agreed.

sentences.zh: 崇遂輕將數十騎馳至上洛，宣詔慰渝，民夷貼然。

translations.literal: Chong then lightly took several dozen horsemen and galloped to Shangluo, proclaiming the edict to comfort and reassure; Han and barbarian alike were content.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong then rode lightly with several dozen horsemen to Shangluo, proclaimed the edict, and reassured the people; Han and tribal subjects alike were calmed.

sentences.zh: 崇命邊戍掠得齊人者悉還之，由是齊人亦還其生口二百許人，二境交和，無復烽燧之警。

translations.literal: Chong ordered that all Qi people captured on the frontier be returned; because of this the Qi also returned about two hundred living captives, the two borders exchanged harmony, and there were no more beacon-fire alarms.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong ordered that all Qi subjects captured on the frontier be returned; in response Qi returned some two hundred captives, the two realms restored peaceful relations, and beacon-fire alarms ceased.

sentences.zh: 久之，徙兗州刺史。

translations.literal: After some time, he was transferred to be Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was transferred to governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 兗土舊多劫盜，崇命村置一樓，樓皆懸鼓，盜發之處，亂擊之；

translations.literal: Yan territory had long had many bandits and robbers; Chong ordered each village to set up a tower, each tower to hang a drum, and wherever bandits appeared to beat them in disorder;
translations.idiomatic: Yan Province had long been plagued by bandits. Li Chong ordered every village to erect a tower with a drum; wherever bandits struck, the drums were beaten in alarm;

sentences.zh: 旁村始聞者，以一擊爲節，次二，次三，俄頃之間，聲布百里；

translations.literal: neighboring villages that first heard would take one beat as the signal, then two, then three; in an instant the sound spread over a hundred li;
translations.idiomatic: neighboring villages relayed the alarm—one beat, then two, then three—and within moments the signal spread a hundred li;

sentences.zh: 皆發人守險要。

translations.literal: all sent men to guard the strategic passes.
translations.idiomatic: and men were dispatched to guard every strategic pass.

sentences.zh: 由是盜發無不擒獲。

translations.literal: Because of this, whenever bandits struck none escaped capture.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter no bandit raid went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 其後諸州皆效之，自崇始也。

translations.literal: Afterward all provinces copied this—it began with Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Later every province adopted the system; Li Chong was its originator.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以征南將軍王僧虔爲左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，以尚書右僕射王奐爲湘州刺史。

translations.literal: On xinwei, General Who Conquers the South Wang Sengqian was made Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Grand General's Staff and Protocol Equal to the Three Dukes, and Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Huan was made Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, General Who Conquers the South Wang Sengqian was appointed Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with a grand general's staff equal to the Three Dukes, and Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Huan was made governor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 宋故建平王景素主簿何昌□、記室王摛及所舉秀才劉璡，前後上書陳景素德美，爲之訟冤。

translations.literal: He Chang□, former chief clerk to Prince Jingsu of Pingping of Song; Wang Chi, recorder; and Liu Zun, a presented scholar whom he had recommended—all successively submitted memorials setting forth Jingsu's virtue and beauty, pleading his case.
translations.idiomatic: He Changyu, former chief clerk to the late Prince Jingsu of Pingping; Wang Chi, his recorder; and Liu Zun, a presented scholar he had recommended—all submitted memorials praising Jingsu's character and pleading his innocence.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛丑，詔聽以士禮還葬舊塋。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinchou, an edict permitted him to be returned and buried in his old tomb mound with the rites due a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on xinchou, an edict permitted Jingsu to be reburied in his original tomb with the rites due a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 璡，□獻之弟也。

translations.literal: Zun was the younger brother of □ Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zun was the younger brother of Liu Xian.

sentences.zh: 十一月，魏高祖將親祀七廟，命有司具儀法，依古制備牲牢、器服及樂章；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the Wei High Ancestor was about to personally sacrifice at the seven ancestral temples; he ordered the officials to prepare the rites, and according to ancient institutions to ready sacrificial animals, vessels and robes, and musical hymns;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, the Wei High Ancestor prepared to sacrifice personally at the seven ancestral temples. He ordered the officials to prepare the rites and, following ancient custom, to ready sacrificial offerings, vessels and vestments, and ceremonial music;

sentences.zh: 自是四時常祀皆舉之。

translations.literal: from this time the regular sacrifices of the four seasons were all performed.
translations.idiomatic: thereafter the regular seasonal sacrifices were all performed.

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝上之上

translations.literal: Emperor Wu the Shizu, Upper Part One.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Shizu, Part One (Upper)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛亥，上祀南郊，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinhai, the Emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar, granted a general amnesty, and changed the reign title.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on xinhai, the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the reign title.

sentences.zh: 詔以邊境寧晏，治民之官，普復田秩。

translations.literal: An edict said that because the borders were peaceful and secure, officials who governed the people should universally have their field stipends restored.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that because the frontiers were at peace, local officials should have their field stipends restored.

sentences.zh: 以太尉豫章王嶷領太子太傅。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Prince Yi of Yuzhang was made concurrent Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Prince Yi of Yuzhang was appointed Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 嶷不參朝務，而常密獻謀畫，上多從之。

translations.literal: Yi did not take part in court affairs, but often secretly presented plans and stratagems, and the Emperor mostly followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Yi did not attend to routine court business, but often submitted confidential counsel, which the emperor usually accepted.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，立皇弟銳爲南平王，鏗爲宜都王，皇子子明爲武昌王，子罕爲南海王。

translations.literal: On renxu, the Emperor's younger brother Rui was established as Prince of Nanping, Keng as Prince of Yidu, the princes Ziming as Prince of Wuchang, and Zihan as Prince of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, the emperor's younger brothers Rui and Keng were enfeoffed as Prince of Nanping and Prince of Yidu, and his sons Ziming and Zihan as Prince of Wuchang and Prince of Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛巳，以征虜將軍楊炅爲沙州刺史、陰平王。

translations.literal: In the second month, on xinsi, General Who Conquers the Barbarians Yang Jiong was made Governor of Sha Province and Prince of Yinping.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinsi, General Who Conquers the Barbarians Yang Jiong was appointed governor of Sha Province and enfeoffed as Prince of Yinping.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以宕昌王梁彌機爲河、涼二州刺史，鄧至王像舒爲西涼州刺史。

translations.literal: On xinchou, King Miji of Dangchang was made Governor of the two provinces of He and Liang, and King Xiangshu of Dengzhi was made Governor of Western Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, King Miji of Dangchang was appointed governor of He and Liang provinces, and King Xiangshu of Dengzhi governor of Western Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 宋末，以治民之官六年過久，乃以三年爲斷，謂之小滿；

translations.literal: At the end of Song, because six years for officials who governed the people was too long, three years was set as the limit, called xiaoman;
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Song dynasty, because six-year terms for local officials were deemed too long, a three-year limit was set, called xiaoman;

sentences.zh: 而遷換去來，又不能依三年之制。

translations.literal: yet transfers and replacements coming and going could not follow the three-year system.
translations.idiomatic: yet in practice transfers and replacements rarely adhered to the three-year rule.

sentences.zh: 三月，癸丑，詔：「自今一以小滿爲限。」

translations.literal: In the third month, on guichou, an edict said: "From now on let xiaoman alone be the limit."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on guichou, an edict declared, "Henceforth the three-year xiaoman term shall be strictly enforced."

sentences.zh: 有司以天文失度，請禳之。

translations.literal: The officials, because celestial signs were out of measure, requested exorcistic rites.
translations.idiomatic: Because the heavens showed irregular portents, the officials requested exorcistic rites.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「應天以實不以文。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "One responds to Heaven with substance, not with ornament.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Heaven is answered with deeds, not with ceremony.

sentences.zh: 我克己求治，思隆惠政；

translations.literal: I restrain myself and seek good governance, thinking to elevate benevolent policies;
translations.idiomatic: I restrain myself and seek good governance, striving to extend benevolent rule;

sentences.zh: 若災眚在我，禳之何益！」

translations.literal: if calamity and blame lie in me, what good would exorcism do!"
translations.idiomatic: if the fault lies with me, what good would exorcism do!"

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬午，昭：「袁粲、劉秉、沈攸之，雖末節不終，而始誠可靈。」

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on renwu, a proclamation said: "Yuan Can, Liu Bing, and Shen Youzhi—though their final conduct did not end well, their initial loyalty deserves to be honored.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on renwu, a proclamation declared, "Yuan Can, Liu Bing, and Shen Youzhi—though their final conduct did not end well, their initial loyalty was genuine and deserves to be remembered.

sentences.zh: 皆命以禮改葬。

translations.literal: All were ordered reburied according to rite.
translations.idiomatic: All three were ordered reburied with proper honors.

sentences.zh: 上之爲太子也，自以年長，與太祖同創大業，朝事大小，率皆專斷，多違制度。

translations.literal: When the Emperor had been Crown Prince, he considered himself older and having with Taizu together founded the great enterprise; matters large and small at court he generally decided on his own, often violating regulations.
translations.idiomatic: As crown prince, he considered himself senior in years and a co-founder of the dynasty with Taizu. He decided most court affairs on his own, often in defiance of established rules.

sentences.zh: 信任左右張景真，景真驕侈，被服什物，僭擬乘輿；

translations.literal: He trusted his attendant Zhang Jingzhen; Jingzhen was arrogant and extravagant—his garments and objects usurped the imperial equipage;
translations.idiomatic: He placed his trust in his attendant Zhang Jingzhen, who grew arrogant and extravagant, dressing and furnishing himself in styles reserved for the emperor;

sentences.zh: 內外畏之，莫敢言者。

translations.literal: inside and outside all feared him; none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: court and palace alike feared him, and no one dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 司空咨議荀伯玉，素爲太祖所親厚，歎曰：「太子所爲，官終不知，豈得畏死，蔽官耳目！

translations.literal: Xun Boyu, consultant to the Minister of Works, had long been treated with affection and favor by Taizu. He sighed and said: "What the Crown Prince does—the court ultimately does not know. How can one fear death and block the court's eyes and ears!
translations.idiomatic: Xun Boyu, consultant to the Minister of Works, had long been favored by Taizu. He sighed and said, "The crown prince's conduct is unknown to the court. How can I fear death and blind the emperor's eyes and ears!

sentences.zh: 我不啟聞，誰當啟者！」

translations.literal: If I do not report it, who will!"
translations.idiomatic: If I do not report it, who will!"

sentences.zh: 因太子拜陵，密以啟太祖。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince went to pay respects at the tombs, he secretly memorialized Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince went to pay respects at the imperial tombs, Boyu secretly reported the matter to Taizu.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒，命檢校東宮。

translations.literal: Taizu was angry and ordered an inspection of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was enraged and ordered an investigation of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 太子拜陵還，至方山，晚，將泊舟，豫章王嶷自東府乘飛燕東迎太子，告以上怒之意。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince returned from paying respects at the tombs; reaching Fangshan in the evening, he was about to moor his boat when Prince Yi of Yuzhang, from the Eastern Palace riding the swift vessel Feiyan, went east to meet the Crown Prince and told him of the Emperor's anger.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was returning from the tombs when, reaching Fangshan at evening and about to moor, Prince Yi of Yuzhang rode the swift vessel Feiyan from the Eastern Palace to meet him and warn him of Taizu's wrath.

sentences.zh: 太子夜歸，入宮，太祖亦停門籥待之。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince returned by night and entered the palace; Taizu also stopped at the gate with the bar drawn, waiting for him.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince returned that night and entered the palace; Taizu waited for him at the barred gate.

sentences.zh: 明日，太祖使南郡王長懋、聞喜公子良宣敕詰責，並示以景真罪狀，使以太子令收景真，殺之。

translations.literal: The next day Taizu sent Prince Changmao of Nanjun and Ziliang, son of the Prince of Wenxi, to proclaim the edict and rebuke him, also showing Jingzhen's crimes, and ordered them by the Crown Prince's command to seize Jingzhen and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Taizu sent Prince Changmao of Nanjun and Ziliang, son of the Prince of Wenxi, to deliver an imperial rebuke, present Zhang Jingzhen's crimes, and by the crown prince's order seize and execute him.

sentences.zh: 太子憂懼，稱疾。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince was anxious and fearful, and claimed illness.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, anxious and afraid, feigned illness.

sentences.zh: 月餘，太祖怒不解，晝臥太陽殿，王敬則直入，叩頭啟太祖曰：「官有天下日淺，太子無事被責，人情恐懼；

translations.literal: After more than a month Taizu's anger had not subsided. He lay resting by day in the Hall of the Grand Sun. Wang Jingze entered directly, kowtowed, and reported to Taizu: "Your Majesty has held the realm only a short while; the Crown Prince has been blamed though innocent—the people fear this;
translations.idiomatic: For more than a month Taizu's wrath did not abate. He spent his days resting in the Hall of the Grand Sun. Wang Jingze went straight in, kowtowed, and pleaded with Taizu: "Your Majesty has held the realm only a short while; the crown prince has been punished without cause, and people everywhere are afraid.

sentences.zh: 願官往東宮解釋之。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would go to the Eastern Palace and explain matters."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to visit the Eastern Palace and set matters right."

sentences.zh: 太祖無言。

translations.literal: Taizu said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said nothing.

sentences.zh: 敬則因大聲宣旨，裝束往東宮，又敕太官設饌，呼左右索輿，太祖了無動意。

translations.literal: Jingze thereupon loudly proclaimed the imperial intent, dressed, and set out for the Eastern Palace; he also ordered the Grand Kitchen to prepare a feast and called attendants to bring the carriage—but Taizu showed not the slightest intention of moving.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze then proclaimed the imperial intent in a loud voice, dressed himself, and set out for the Eastern Palace. He ordered the imperial kitchen to prepare a feast and summoned attendants to bring the carriage, but Taizu showed no sign of moving.

sentences.zh: 敬則索衣被太祖，乃牽強登輿。

translations.literal: Jingze fetched clothes and draped Taizu, then forcibly helped him into the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze fetched clothes and dressed Taizu, then practically dragged him into the carriage.

sentences.zh: 太祖不得已至東宮，召諸王宴於玄圃。

translations.literal: Taizu, having no choice, arrived at the Eastern Palace and summoned the princes to a banquet in the Xuan Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu reluctantly went to the Eastern Palace and summoned the princes to a banquet in the Mystic Garden.

sentences.zh: 長沙王晃捉華蓋，臨川王映執雉尾扇，聞喜公子良持酒鎗，南郡王長懋行酒，太子及豫章王嶷、王敬則自捧酒饌，至暮，盡醉乃還。

translations.literal: Prince Huang of Changsha held the imperial canopy; Prince Ying of Linchuan held the pheasant-tail fan; Ziliang, son of the Prince of Wenxi, carried the wine ladle; Prince Changmao of Nanjun circulated the wine; the Crown Prince, Prince Yi of Yuzhang, and Wang Jingze personally served wine and food. They drank until evening and returned thoroughly drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huang of Changsha held the imperial canopy; Prince Ying of Linchuan carried the pheasant-tail fan; Ziliang, son of the Prince of Wenxi, bore the wine ladle; Prince Changmao of Nanjun poured the wine; and the crown prince, Prince Yi of Yuzhang, and Wang Jingze personally served the food and drink. They feasted until evening and returned utterly drunk.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉伯玉忠藎，愈見親信，軍國密事，多委使之，權動朝右。

translations.literal: Taizu praised Boyu for his loyal devotion, trusted him all the more, entrusted him with many secret military and state affairs, and his authority shook the right flank of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu praised Boyu for his loyal devotion and trusted him all the more. He entrusted him with many secret matters of war and state, and Boyu's power came to rival the highest ministers at court.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，去宅二里許，冠蓋已塞路。

translations.literal: When he suffered his mother's bereavement, less than two li from his residence the road was already blocked with officials' carriages.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, the road was already choked with officials' carriages less than two li from his home.

sentences.zh: 左率蕭景先、侍中王晏共吊之，自旦至暮，始得前。

translations.literal: Left Leader Xiao Jingxian and Palace Attendant Wang Yan together went to offer condolences; from dawn to dusk they only then were able to reach him.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard Commander Xiao Jingxian and Palace Attendant Wang Yan went together to offer condolences. From dawn until dusk they could barely get through to him.

sentences.zh: 比出，饑乏，氣息惙然，憤悒形於聲貌。

translations.literal: When they finally emerged, they were hungry and exhausted, gasping feebly; anger and vexation showed in voice and countenance.
translations.idiomatic: When they finally got out, they were hungry and exhausted, barely able to catch their breath; their anger and dismay showed plainly in voice and face.

sentences.zh: 明日，言於太祖曰：「臣等所見二宮門庭，比荀伯玉宅可張雀羅矣。」

translations.literal: The next day they said to Taizu: "The gate courtyards of both palaces that we saw could spread bird nets, compared with Xun Boyu's residence."
translations.idiomatic: The next day they told Taizu: "The courtyards at both palaces were so empty you could spread nets for birds there—unlike the crush at Xun Boyu's house."

sentences.zh: 晏，敬弘之從子也。

translations.literal: Yan was a nephew of Jinghong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan was a nephew of Wang Jinghong.

sentences.zh: 驍騎將軍陳胤叔，先亦白景真及太子得失，而語太子皆云「伯玉以聞」。

translations.literal: Cavalry General Chen Yinshu had also earlier reported Jingzhen's misconduct and the Crown Prince's lapses to the emperor, yet in speaking with the Crown Prince always said "Boyu reported it."
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry General Chen Yinshu had also reported Jingzhen's misconduct and the crown prince's failings to the emperor, yet whenever he spoke to the crown prince he said only, "Boyu reported it."

sentences.zh: 太子由是深怨伯玉。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince therefore deeply resented Boyu.
translations.idiomatic: From this the crown prince came to hate Boyu bitterly.
