sentences.zh: 太祖陰有以豫章王嶷代太子之意，而嶷事太子愈謹，故太子友愛不衰。

translations.literal: Taizu secretly had in mind replacing the Crown Prince with Prince Yi of Yuzhang, but Yi served the Crown Prince with growing diligence, so the Crown Prince's affection did not fade.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu secretly considered replacing the crown prince with Prince Yi of Yuzhang, but Yi grew ever more devoted in serving the crown prince, so their bond of affection never weakened.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史垣崇祖不親附太子，會崇祖破魏兵，太祖召還朝，與之密謀。

translations.literal: Yuan Chongzu, Inspector of Yuzhou, did not draw close to the Crown Prince. When Chongzu defeated Wei troops, Taizu summoned him back to court and conspired with him in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chongzu, provincial inspector of Yuzhou, had never been close to the crown prince. After Chongzu defeated Wei forces, Taizu recalled him to court and took him into his confidence.

sentences.zh: 太子疑之，曲加禮待，謂曰：「世間流言，我已豁懷；

translations.literal: The Crown Prince suspected him and with elaborate courtesy treated him well, saying: "Rumors in the world—I have already opened my heart regarding them;
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince suspected him but treated him with elaborate courtesy, saying, "As for the rumors in the world, I have put them out of my mind.

sentences.zh: 自今以富貴相付。」

translations.literal: From now on I entrust wealth and honor to you."
translations.idiomatic: From now on I entrust wealth and honor to you."

sentences.zh: 崇祖拜謝。

translations.literal: Chongzu bowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzu bowed his thanks.

sentences.zh: 會太祖復遣荀伯玉，敕以邊事，受旨夜發，不得辭東宮；

translations.literal: Just then Taizu again sent Xun Boyu with orders on frontier affairs; receiving the edict he set out by night and could not take leave at the Eastern Palace;
translations.idiomatic: Just then Taizu again dispatched Xun Boyu with orders on frontier affairs. Boyu received the edict and set out that very night without taking leave at the Eastern Palace;

sentences.zh: 太子以爲不盡誠，益銜之。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince considered him not fully sincere and harbored resentment all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince took this as a lack of sincerity and resented him all the more.

sentences.zh: 太祖臨終，指伯玉以屬太子。

translations.literal: As Taizu approached death, he pointed to Boyu and entrusted him to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Taizu pointed to Boyu and commended him to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 上即位，崇祖累遷五兵尚書，伯玉累遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When the Emperor ascended the throne, Chongzu was repeatedly promoted to Minister of the Five Arms, Boyu repeatedly promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Chongzu rose to Minister of the Five Arms, and Boyu rose to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 伯玉內懷憂懼，上以伯玉與崇祖善，恐其爲變，加意撫之。

translations.literal: Boyu inwardly harbored anxiety and fear; the Emperor, because Boyu was on good terms with Chongzu, feared they might cause trouble and treated him with special solicitude.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu was inwardly anxious and afraid. The emperor knew Boyu was close to Chongzu and feared they might rise in rebellion, so he treated Boyu with extra care.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，下詔誣崇祖招結江北荒人，欲與伯玉作亂，皆收殺之。

translations.literal: On dinghai, an edict was issued falsely charging that Chongzu had gathered homeless people north of the river and wished to rebel with Boyu; both were seized and killed.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai the emperor issued an edict falsely accusing Chongzu of recruiting refugees north of the Yangzi to rebel with Boyu. Both men were seized and executed.

sentences.zh: 庚子，魏主如崞山；

translations.literal: On gengzi the Wei emperor went to Mount Guo;
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the Wei emperor went to Mount Guo;

sentences.zh: 壬寅，還宮。

translations.literal: On renyin he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 閏月，癸丑，魏主後宮平涼林氏生子恂，大赦。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on guichou, Consort Lin of Pingliang in the Wei emperor's harem bore a son, Xun, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on guichou, Consort Lin of Pingliang in the Wei emperor's harem gave birth to a son named Xun, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 文明太后以恂當爲太子，賜林氏死，自撫養恂。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming, because Xun was to be crown prince, granted Lin death and personally reared Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming, intending Xun as heir, ordered Lin put to death and raised the child herself.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊寅朔，魏主如武州山石窟佛寺。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the first day wuyin, the Wei emperor went to the stone-cave Buddhist temple on Mount Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the first day wuyin, the Wei emperor visited the cliff-temple at Mount Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍張敬兒好信夢。

translations.literal: Chariots-and-Cavalry General Zhang Jinger was fond of believing dreams.
translations.idiomatic: Chariots-and-Cavalry General Zhang Jinger was a great believer in dreams.

sentences.zh: 初爲南陽太守，其妻尚氏夢一手熱如火；

translations.literal: When he was first Administrator of Nanyang, his wife Lady Shang dreamed one hand hot as fire;
translations.idiomatic: When he was first administrator of Nanyang, his wife Lady Shang dreamed that one of her hands burned hot as fire;

sentences.zh: 及爲雍州，夢一胛熱；

translations.literal: When he became Governor of Yongzhou, she dreamed one shoulder blade hot;
translations.idiomatic: When he became governor of Yongzhou, she dreamed one shoulder blade was burning;

sentences.zh: 爲開府，夢半身熱。

translations.literal: When he opened a headquarters as Grand General, she dreamed half the body hot.
translations.idiomatic: When he opened a grand headquarters, she dreamed half her body was hot.

sentences.zh: 敬兒意欲無限，當謂所親曰：「吾妻復夢舉體熱矣。」

translations.literal: Jinger's ambitions were boundless; he once said to those close to him: "My wife has again dreamed her whole body hot."
translations.idiomatic: Jinger's ambitions knew no limit. He once told his intimates, "My wife has dreamed her whole body was hot again."

sentences.zh: 又自言夢舊村社樹高至天，上聞而惡之。

translations.literal: He also said himself that he dreamed the village altar tree of his old home reached to heaven; when the Emperor heard he detested it.
translations.idiomatic: He also said he had dreamed the village altar tree of his hometown reached to the sky. When the emperor heard this he took offense.

sentences.zh: 垣崇祖死，敬兒內自疑，會有人告敬兒遣人至蠻中貨易，上疑其有異志。

translations.literal: When Yuan Chongzu died, Jinger inwardly suspected himself; just then someone reported that Jinger had sent men to the barbarian regions to trade, and the Emperor suspected he harbored disloyal intent.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Chongzu's death Jinger grew uneasy. Someone then reported that he had sent men into the tribal lands to trade, and the emperor suspected him of rebellious intent.

sentences.zh: 會上於華林園設八關齋，朝臣皆預，於坐收敬兒。

translations.literal: Just then the Emperor held the Eight Precepts fast at Hualin Garden; all court ministers attended, and at the assembly Jinger was seized.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor happened to be holding an Eight Precepts assembly at Hualin Garden with all the ministers present. Jinger was seized on the spot.

sentences.zh: 敬兒脫冠貂投地曰：「此物誤我！」

translations.literal: Jinger removed his sable-trimmed official cap and threw it to the ground, saying: "This thing ruined me!"
translations.idiomatic: Jinger tore off his official cap trimmed with sable and flung it to the ground. "This thing ruined me!"

sentences.zh: 丁酉，殺敬兒，並其四子。

translations.literal: On dingyou Jinger was killed, together with his four sons.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou Jinger was executed, together with his four sons.

sentences.zh: 敬兒弟恭兒，常慮爲兄禍所及，居於冠軍，未常出襄陽，村落深阻，牆垣重複。

translations.literal: Jinger's younger brother Gong'er always feared being swept up in his brother's disaster; he lived in Guanjun and never left Xiangyang—the village was deep and blocked, its walls layered in repetition.
translations.idiomatic: Jinger's younger brother Gong'er always feared being caught up in his brother's downfall. He lived at Guanjun and never left Xiangyang. His hamlet lay in deep country, ringed with repeated walls.

sentences.zh: 敬兒每遣信，輒上馬屬鞬，然後見之。

translations.literal: Whenever Jinger sent a messenger, Gong'er would immediately mount his horse with bow and quiver at the saddle, then only afterward receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Jinger sent a messenger, Gong'er would mount his horse with bow at the saddle before he would receive him.

sentences.zh: 敬兒敗問至，席捲入蠻；

translations.literal: When news of Jinger's defeat arrived, he packed up and fled into the barbarian regions;
translations.idiomatic: When news of Jinger's downfall arrived, he packed up and fled into the tribal lands;

sentences.zh: 後自出，上恕之。

translations.literal: Afterward he came out on his own; the Emperor pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He later came out of hiding on his own, and the emperor pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 敬兒女爲征北咨議參軍謝超宗子婦，超宗謂丹陽尹李安民曰：「『往年殺韓信，今年殺彭越。』

translations.literal: Jinger's daughter was the daughter-in-law of Xie Chaozong, Military Advisor to the Campaign-north General. Chaozong said to Li Anmin, Prefect of Danyang: "'Last year Han Xin was killed; this year Peng Yue is killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jinger's daughter was married to the son of Xie Chaozong, advisor to the northern campaign staff. Chaozong said to Li Anmin, prefect of Danyang, "Last year they killed Han Xin; this year they kill Peng Yue.

sentences.zh: 尹欲何計！」

translations.literal: Prefect, what plan do you intend!"
translations.idiomatic: Prefect, what do you plan to do!"

sentences.zh: 安民具啟之。

translations.literal: Anmin fully reported this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Anmin reported the whole matter to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上素惡超宗輕慢，使兼御史中丞袁彖奏彈超宗，丁巳，收付廷尉，徙越巂，於道賜死。

translations.literal: The Emperor had long disliked Chaozong's levity and disrespect; he had Supervising Censor Yuan Tan impeach Chaozong. On dingsi Chaozong was seized and handed to the Court of Justice, exiled to Yuexi, and granted death on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long disliked Chaozong's insolence. He had Supervising Censor Yuan Tan impeach him. On dingsi Chaozong was arrested and handed to the Court of Justice, exiled to Yuexi, and ordered to die on the road.

sentences.zh: 以彖語不刻切，又使左丞王逡之奏彈彖輕文略奏，撓法容非，彖坐免官，禁錮十年。

translations.literal: Because Tan's language was not sharp enough, the Emperor also had Left Assistant Wang Xunzhi impeach Tan for slight wording and abbreviated memorial, bending the law and tolerating wrongdoing; Tan was punished by removal from office and ten years' confinement.
translations.idiomatic: Because Tan's wording was not cutting enough, the emperor had Left Assistant Wang Xunzhi impeach Tan for a lenient, perfunctory memorial that indulged wrongdoing. Tan was dismissed from office and placed under confinement for ten years.

sentences.zh: 超宗，靈運之孫；

translations.literal: Chaozong was the grandson of Lingyun;
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong was the grandson of Xie Lingyun;

sentences.zh: 彖，顗之弟子也。

translations.literal: Tan was a disciple-nephew of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was a nephew-disciple of Yuan Yi.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁丑，魏主及太后如神淵池。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on dingchou, the Wei emperor and the Empress Dowager went to the Shenyuan Pool.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on dingchou, the Wei emperor and the empress dowager went to Shenyuan Pool.

sentences.zh: 甲申，如方山。

translations.literal: On jiashen they went to Mount Fang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen they went to Mount Fang.

sentences.zh: 魏使假員外散騎常侍頓丘李彪來聘。

translations.literal: Wei sent Acting Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Li Biao of Dunqiu on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent Li Biao of Dunqiu, acting regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, on a diplomatic visit.

sentences.zh: 侍中、左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司王僧虔固辭開府，謂兄子儉曰：「汝任重於朝，行登三事；

translations.literal: Palace Attendant, Left Grand Master of the Brilliant Hall, and Grand General with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes Wang Sengqian firmly declined opening a headquarters, saying to his brother's son Jian: "You bear heavy responsibility at court and will soon reach the Three Excellencies;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Wang Sengqian, left grand master of the Brilliant Hall and grand general with staff equal to the three dukes, firmly declined to open a grand headquarters. He told his nephew Jian, "You bear heavy duties at court and are on your way to the three highest offices.

sentences.zh: 我若復有此授，乃是一門有二台司，吾實懼焉。」

translations.literal: If I again received such an appointment, it would mean one clan holding two positions among the Three Excellencies—I truly fear this."
translations.idiomatic: If I were given such an appointment as well, our house would hold two of the highest posts. That frightens me."

sentences.zh: 累年不拜，上乃許之，戊戌，加僧虔特進。

translations.literal: For years he would not accept; the Emperor then permitted it. On wuxu Sengqian was given the title Special Advance.
translations.idiomatic: For years he refused to accept. The emperor finally allowed it, and on wuxu Sengqian was granted the rank of special advancement.

sentences.zh: 儉作長梁齋，制度小過，僧虔視之，不悅，竟不入戶；

translations.literal: Jian built the Long Beam Study; its dimensions were slightly excessive. Sengqian viewed it, was displeased, and would not enter the door;
translations.idiomatic: Jian built a Long Beam Study whose dimensions exceeded proper bounds. Sengqian looked it over, displeased, and would not step inside;

sentences.zh: 儉即日毀之。

translations.literal: Jian that same day demolished it.
translations.idiomatic: Jian demolished it that very day.

sentences.zh: 初，王弘與兄弟集會，任子孫戲適。

translations.literal: In the beginning, when Wang Hong gathered with his brothers, he let the grandchildren play freely.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, when Wang Hong gathered with his brothers, he let the grandchildren play as they pleased.

sentences.zh: 僧達跳下地作虎子；

translations.literal: Sengda leaped to the ground and played the tiger cub;
translations.idiomatic: Sengda leapt to the floor and crouched like a tiger cub;

sentences.zh: 僧綽正坐，采蠟燭珠爲鳳皇，僧達奪取打壞，亦復不惜；

translations.literal: Sengchuo sat upright, gathering wax candle beads to make a phoenix; Sengda snatched and smashed it, yet did not mind at all;
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo sat properly, gathering wax beads from candles to shape a phoenix. Sengda snatched it away and smashed it, yet Sengchuo did not care in the least;

sentences.zh: 僧虔累十二博棋，既不墜落，亦不重作。

translations.literal: Sengqian stacked twelve game stones; they neither fell nor did he rebuild them.
translations.idiomatic: Sengqian stacked twelve game pieces without letting them fall, and never tried to rebuild a fallen stack.

sentences.zh: 弘歎曰：「僧達俊爽，當不減人，然恐終危吾家；

translations.literal: Hong sighed and said: "Sengda is brilliant and bold—he will surely not fall short of others, yet I fear he will in the end endanger our house;
translations.idiomatic: Hong sighed and said, "Sengda is brilliant and bold and will not fall short of others, yet I fear he will bring ruin to our house in the end.

sentences.zh: 僧綽當以名義見美；

translations.literal: Sengchuo will be admired for reputation and principle;
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo will be honored for his reputation and integrity;

sentences.zh: 僧虔必爲長者，位至公台。」

translations.literal: Sengqian will surely become the clan elder and rise to the highest offices."
translations.idiomatic: Sengqian will surely become the steady elder of the clan and rise to the highest offices."

sentences.zh: 已而皆如其言。

translations.literal: In time all came to pass as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: In time everything happened just as he had said.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚申，驍騎將軍王洪範自柔然還，經塗三萬餘里。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on gengshen, Cavalry General Wang Hongfan returned from Rouran, having traveled more than thirty thousand li on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on gengshen, Cavalry General Wang Hongfan returned from the Rouran, having traveled more than thirty thousand li.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙寅，遭驍騎將軍劉纘聘於魏，魏主客令李安世主之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on bingyin, Cavalry General Liu Zuan was dispatched on a friendly mission to Wei; the Wei chief of reception Li Anshi hosted him.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on bingyin, the court dispatched Cavalry General Liu Zuan as envoy to Wei. Li Anshi, chief of reception for foreign envoys, hosted him.

sentences.zh: 魏人出內藏之寶，使賈人鬻之於市。

translations.literal: The Wei people brought out treasures from the inner storehouse and had merchants sell them in the market.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei brought treasures from the imperial vaults and had merchants sell them in the markets.

sentences.zh: 纘曰：「魏金玉大賤，當由山川所出。」

translations.literal: Zuan said: "Wei's gold and jade are very cheap—this must be because they come forth from mountains and rivers."
translations.idiomatic: Zuan said, "Gold and jade are so cheap in Wei—it must be because they come straight from the mountains and rivers."

sentences.zh: 安世曰：「聖朝不貴金玉，故賤同瓦礫。」

translations.literal: Anshi said: "The sage court does not prize gold and jade, hence they are cheap as tiles and rubble."
translations.idiomatic: Anshi said, "Our sacred court does not value gold and jade, so they are priced no higher than tiles and rubble."

sentences.zh: 纘初欲多市，聞其言，內慚而止。

translations.literal: Zuan had at first wished to buy many; hearing this speech, he was inwardly ashamed and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan had meant to buy heavily, but hearing this he felt ashamed and gave up the idea.

sentences.zh: 纘屢奉使至魏，馮太后遂私幸之。

translations.literal: Zuan repeatedly served as envoy to Wei, and Empress Dowager Feng then privately favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zuan served repeatedly as envoy to Wei, and Empress Dowager Feng took him as her private lover.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙巳朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day yisi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the first day yisi, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，魏始禁同姓爲婚。

translations.literal: On guichou Wei first prohibited marriage between people of the same surname.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Wei first prohibited marriage between people of the same clan name.

sentences.zh: 王儉進號衛將軍，參掌選事。

translations.literal: Wang Jian was promoted to the title Guards General and shared in charge of selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian was promoted to Guards General and given a share in appointments.

sentences.zh: 是歲，省巴州。

translations.literal: That year Bazhou was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: That year the court abolished Bazhou province.

sentences.zh: 魏秦州刺史於洛侯，性殘酷，刑人或斷腕，拔舌，分懸四體。

translations.literal: Yu Luohou, Inspector of Qinzhou in Wei, was by nature cruel and fierce; in punishing people he would sever wrists, pull out tongues, or suspend the four limbs separately.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Luohou, Wei inspector of Qin province, was cruel by nature. He punished people by severing wrists, pulling out tongues, or hanging the four limbs apart.

sentences.zh: 合州驚駭，州民王元壽等一時俱反。

translations.literal: The whole province was shocked and terrified; the provincial people Wang Yuanshou and others all rebelled at once.
translations.idiomatic: The whole province was horrified. Wang Yuanshou and other locals rose in rebellion at once.

sentences.zh: 有司劾奏之，魏主遣使至州，於洛侯常刑人處宣告吏民，然後斬之。

translations.literal: The responsible offices impeached and memorialized him; the Wei emperor sent an envoy to the province, at the place where Luohou customarily punished people proclaimed this to officials and people, then beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities impeached him. The Wei emperor sent an envoy to the province, proclaimed Luohou's crimes to officials and people at the place where he usually executed men, and then had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 齊州刺史韓麒麟，爲政尚寬，從事劉普慶説麒麟曰：「公杖節方夏，而無所誅斬，何以示威！」

translations.literal: Han Qilin, Inspector of Qizhou, in governing favored leniency. Staff member Liu Puqing urged Qilin: "Sir, you hold the staff of authority in high summer, yet have executed and beheaded no one—how can you display authority!"
translations.idiomatic: Han Qilin, inspector of Qi province, governed with leniency. A staff officer Liu Puqing urged him, "Sir, you hold imperial authority in the height of summer yet have executed no one—how can you show your power!"

sentences.zh: 麒麟曰：「刑罰所以止惡，仁者不得已而用之。

translations.literal: Qilin said: "Punishments exist to stop evil; the humane use them only when they have no choice.
translations.idiomatic: Qilin said, "Punishment exists to stop wrongdoing. Humane men use it only when they must.

sentences.zh: 今民不犯法，又何誅乎？

translations.literal: Now the people do not violate the law—why execute anyone?
translations.idiomatic: The people are not breaking the law—why should I execute anyone?

sentences.zh: 若必斷斬然後可以立威，當以卿應之！」

translations.literal: If executions and beheadings are required before authority can be established, then you should serve as the example!"
translations.idiomatic: If beheadings are what it takes to establish authority, then you should supply the example!"

sentences.zh: 普慶慚懼而起。

translations.literal: Puqing, ashamed and fearful, rose.
translations.idiomatic: Puqing rose, ashamed and afraid.
